the shader. A `defines` key never appears as a field on the expanded pass
object itself; only the resulting `program` name changes.

`repeat` is resolved at execution. A number becomes
`max(1,floor(repeat))`. A string looks up `globalUniforms[name]`, then
`pass.uniforms[name]`. Numeric values use `max(1,floor(value))`, otherwise one.
Repeated writes advance frame-local ping-pong bindings after every iteration.

`drawBuffers > 1` or more than one output activates MRT. `blend: true` is
additive one/one. A two-item blend array selects explicit factors. Unknown
WebGL factors fall back to `ONE`. WebGPU lowercases/replaces underscores and
lets device validation reject invalid factors.

Before surface allocation, the pipeline sums the color-attachment byte cost of every multi-output pass in output insertion order.
The costs are:

- `rgba32f` and `rgba32float`: 16 bytes.
- `rgba8` and `rgba8unorm`: 4 bytes.
- Every other or missing format: 8 bytes.

If the sum exceeds `capabilities.maxColorBytesPerSample`, the pipeline examines attachments from last to first.
It changes only `rgba32f`/`rgba32float` specs to `rgba16f`, subtracting 8 per change.
It stops when the group fits or no eligible attachment remains. This mutates
`graph.textures` before allocation and deliberately preserves the precision of
earlier attachments. It is a best-effort adaptation, not an admission check:
an over-budget group with insufficient demotable attachments remains
over-budget and emits no structured failure.

Fresh allocation uses the mutated graph format. Texture reuse requires matching
dimensions and format. A 3D texture must also have matching depth. A
double-buffered global surface must have matching read and write textures.
The pipeline recreates the allocation when one of these properties differs.

Inspect `pipeline.backend.textures` to verify the physical formats. Do not use
only `graph.textures` as evidence. A framebuffer failure surfaces through the structured, non-throwing
`backend.diagnostics` records (`ERR_MISSING_RENDER_TARGET` for missing FBO/MRT
targets, `ERR_GL_ERROR` for post-draw drained `gl.getError()` failures; console
output unchanged).

`type` does not select a WebGPU compute program. WebGPU detects a compute-only
program from `@compute` without `@fragment`. WebGL detects compute-style work
from `storageTextures` or an `outputBuffer` output and applies a fragment-pass
fallback.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` - pass construction and input/output
mapping, `defines`-suffixed program-variant construction; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `render()`,
`resolveRepeatCount()`, `applyMrtFormatBudget()`, `shouldSkipPass()`; backend `executePass()` and
blend resolvers.

### Validate

A source-grounded graph gate can assert:

```text
semantic_error_count === 0
expansion_error_count === 0
passes.length >= 1
renderSurface !== null
every pass.program resolves in graph.programs
every pass output is a nonempty string
every pass input is a nonempty string or intentionally omitted for null arg
every non-global produced texture has an allocations entry
```

`analyzeLiveness(passes)` returns `{start,end}` indices for every non-`global_`
texture touched as an input or output. Both indices are in
`[0, passes.length-1]` and `start <= end`. `allocateResources()` assigns
`phys_0`, `phys_1`, ... to non-global outputs and reuses a slot only when its
previous texture's `end < currentPassIndex`.

The allocation map is consumed by the renderer behind the explicit
`texturePooling: true` opt-in.
`Pipeline.buildTexturePoolingPlan()` reads `graph.allocations` and groups
virtual textures that share a physical slot; `Pipeline.recreateTextures()`
creates one backend texture per group under the group's primary id and aliases
the other members' backend map entries to it, so every pass binds the shared
record through either id. A group is pooled only when every member carries an
identical plain 2D spec (no `persistent`, `mipmaps`, or 3D policy) and each
member's first touch in the pass list is a producing write that does not
sample the texture itself, and no member is written by a partial/non-clearing
pass (any explicit `drawMode` scatter or `blend`, or a `viewport` write without
`clear: true`, which exposes a group-mate's content in the unwritten region) —
first-read and
cross-frame accumulation semantics match standalone textures; the default
(opt-out) pipeline keeps one backend texture per virtual id.
`Pipeline.getResourcePlan()` reports both the analyzer's physical allocation
map and the sharing the renderer actually materialized (`pooling`,
`allocations`, `sharedTextures`, `textures` with per-record
`virtualTextures`).

There is no dependency/cycle validator. A pass that reads a texture before a
producer can compile and may sample a default, stale, or missing texture. A
formal authoring gate must perform its own source-order check:

```text
For each non-global, non-external input at pass i:
  some pass j < i must produce it, OR it must be intentionally frame-persistent.
```

That predicate is recommended policy, not an engine-emitted result.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/resources.js` - liveness/allocation;
`shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `buildTexturePoolingPlan()` and
`getResourcePlan()`, which consume `graph.allocations`; backend texture
binding fallbacks.

### Diagnose

Expansion uses `ExpansionFailure`. Graph/backend failures include:

```ts
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_SPEC_MISSING", program: string, pass: string }
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND", program: string, pass: string }
{ code: "ERR_TEXTURE_NOT_FOUND", texture: string, pass: string } // WebGPU
{ code: "ERR_NO_MRT_OUTPUTS", pass: string }                     // WebGPU
{ code: "ERR_COMPUTE_DISPATCH_UNRESOLVED", pass: string,
  detail: "Compute dispatch dimensions could not be inferred" }
```

WebGL2 missing FBOs and MRT textures are console warnings, not throws. WebGL
errors discovered after a draw are logged with pass/effect/program/output/input
context and drained; each drained error is also recorded as an `ERR_GL_ERROR`
diagnostic. WebGPU missing MRT members, a missing render-surface storage
target (which falls back to a temporary storage texture) and a missing
buffer-copy output are console warnings. Device validation arrives as an
`uncapturederror` console message. All of these paths also record structured,
non-throwing diagnostics in the backend's `backend.diagnostics` collector
(`ERR_MISSING_RENDER_TARGET` with `kind` `fbo`/`mrt` on WebGL2 and
`mrt`/`storage-surface`/`copy-output` on WebGPU, `ERR_GL_ERROR`,
`ERR_DEVICE_VALIDATION`; console output unchanged).

Definition fields `name`, `viewport`, `clear`, `samplerTypes`, and `type` are
copied by `expand()` onto the expanded passes. `conditions` reaches
`Pipeline.shouldSkipPass()` (the mechanism
this round's per-`viewMode`/`blendMode` pass-cloning pattern relies on to
select which cloned pass variant actually runs). `viewport` is resolved per
frame into `viewportResolved` {x, y, w, h} numbers by
`Pipeline.resolvePassViewport()` (the authored spec stays on `viewport`), and
the backends prefer the resolved numbers with output-texture dimensions still
taking priority. `clear` reaches the WebGPU render-pass loadOp and
`samplerTypes` the WebGPU per-binding sampler selection. `name` and `type`
are queryable pass labels: backend shader-kind dispatch remains
source-derived, so `type` has no behavioral consumer on the expanded pass.
`inputOverride` on dimension specs is accepted but unconsumed.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `compilePrograms()`, `render()`,
`shouldSkipPass()`; backend `executePass()` implementations;
`shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` - constructed pass keys.

<!-- SURFACE:TEXTURES -->
## Textures and surface resources

### Introspect

Definition texture specs are available at `effect.textures` (2D) and, for
class-based effects, `effect.textures3d`. Expanded/scoped specs are returned in
`graph.textures: Map<string,RuntimeTextureSpec>`. Allocated backend records are
in `pipeline.backend.textures`. Double-buffer records are in
`pipeline.surfaces`.

```ts
type RuntimeTextureSpec = {
  width: DimensionSpec
  height: DimensionSpec
  depth?: DimensionSpec
  format: string
  is3D?: boolean
  usage: Array<"render" | "sample" | "storage" | "copySrc" | "copyDst">
}

type SurfaceRecord2D = {
  read: string
  write: string
  currentFrame: number
}

type MeshSurfaceRecord = {
  positions: string
  normals: string
  uvs: string
  width: number
  height: number
}

type DeviceCapabilities = {
  isMobile: boolean
  floatBlend: boolean
  floatLinear: boolean
  colorBufferFloat: boolean
  maxDrawBuffers: number
  maxTextureSize: number
  maxColorBytesPerSample: number | undefined
  maxStateSize: number
}
```

Node-local texture names are prefixed with `node_<step>_`. Non-particle names
beginning `global_` are chain-scoped. Particle state names are scoped to the
creating particle node. Normal global surfaces have `_read`/`_write` backend
textures.

`pipeline.getCapabilities()` returns the active backend object.
`CanvasRenderer.capabilities` delegates to it. Before a pipeline/backend is
available, both public paths use `maxDrawBuffers:8`, `maxTextureSize:4096`,
`maxColorBytesPerSample:64`, and `maxStateSize:2048` with all float flags true
and `isMobile:false`.

An initialized WebGL2 backend reads draw-buffer and
texture limits from GL. When `EXT_color_buffer_float` exists, it probes tiny
MRT groups and reports one of `64`, `48`, `40`, `32`, or the fallback `16`.
Without that extension its byte budget is `undefined`.

WebGPU reports
`device.limits.maxTextureDimension2D || 8192` and
`device.limits.maxColorAttachmentBytesPerSample || 32`. Both backends use
`maxStateSize:512` on detected mobile devices and `2048` otherwise.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` - texture-spec collection/scoping;
`shaders/src/runtime/compiler.js` - `extractTextureSpecs()`;
`shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `getCapabilities()`, `createSurfaces()`,
`recreateTextures()`; `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - `capabilities`;
backend `init()` methods.

### Act

```ts
type DimensionSpec =
  | number
  | "screen"
  | "auto"
  | "input"        // resolves to the screen size
  | "resolution"   // resolves to the screen size
  | `${number}%`
  | { param: string, paramDefault?: number, multiply?: number,
      power?: number, default?: number }
  | { screenDivide: string, default?: number }
  | { scale: number, clamp?: { min?: number, max?: number } }

// The formats validateEffectDefinition() accepts: those both backends resolve.
type TextureFormat2D =
  | "rgba8" | "rgba16f" | "rgba32f"
  | "r8" | "r16f" | "r32f"
  | "rgba8unorm" | "rgba16float" | "rgba32float"
  | "r8unorm" | "r16float" | "r32float"

interface TextureSpec2D {
  width?: DimensionSpec
  height?: DimensionSpec
  format?: TextureFormat2D
}

interface TextureSpec3D extends TextureSpec2D {
  depth?: DimensionSpec
}

type TextureSpec = TextureSpec2D | TextureSpec3D
```

Omitted/falsy definition width or height becomes `screen`. Omitted format
becomes `rgba16f`. Graph-generated pass outputs also use screen size,
`rgba16f`, and usage `render/sample/copySrc/copyDst`. A 3D spec gets
`is3D:true`. Its depth default is `effectSpec.depth || effectSpec.width || 64`
and usage is `storage/sample/copySrc/copyDst`.

Dimension resolution:

| Spec | Resolved pixels |
|---|---|
| number | `max(1,floor(spec))` |
| `screen` / `auto` | the corresponding pipeline screen dimension |
| percentage string | `max(1,floor(screenSize * parseFloat(spec)/100))` |
| `{param}` | uniform value or `paramDefault` or 64. Then multiply/power. Transformed missing-param can use final `default`. Floor and clamp to at least 1 |
| `{screenDivide}` | `max(1,round(screenSize/(uniform or default or 1)))` |
| `{scale}` | floor of screenSizexscale, optional min/max clamp, then at least 1 |
| any other value/string | screen size |

`expand()` also follows a volume/geometry surface's dimensions through
`write3d()`/`read3d()` handoffs, so a later chain that reads a previously
exported `volN`/`geoN` (via `read3d(volN)`/`read3d(geoN)`, not the producing
chain's own local reference) inherits that surface's actual size instead of
defaulting to 64. It tracks, per expansion: every chain-scoped
`volumeSize_<chainScope>` parameter a `write3d()` call last wrote (and the
numeric value it wrote), every `read3d()` call's producer surface and scope,
and every surface a `write3d()`/`write3d`-adjacent geometry blit exports to.
After all plans expand, it resolves each reader's scope to its writer
(following re-exports and repeated same-surface filters transitively, with
cycle protection), rewrites that reader's `textureSpecs` width/height/depth
to reference the resolved writer's sizing parameter, and rewrites any pass
uniform still holding the reader's own placeholder parameter name to the
resolved writer's parameter and value. A `volN`/`geoN` surface with no
preceding `write3d()` in the compiled program is unaffected and keeps its
default sizing (64 for volumes, screen-sized for geometry).

Before each `createSurfaces()` allocation pass, numeric uniforms named exactly
`volumeSize` or starting with `volumeSize_chain_`/`volumeSize_node_` are
clamped against `capabilities.maxTextureSize`. A value whose square fits is
unchanged. Otherwise, the algorithm starts at 16.
It doubles while the next power of two satisfies both conditions:

- It remains below the requested value.
- Its square is no larger than the texture limit.

Thus `128` becomes `64` for an `8192` limit and `32`
for a `2048` limit. A missing/falsy limit or a nonnumeric automation value is
left untouched. The pipeline mutates every affected pass uniform before
dimension resolution and warns only once per requested-to-effective pair.

The same clamp applies to `Pipeline.setUniform()` for unscoped, chain-scoped,
and node-scoped names. `CanvasRenderer.applyStepParameterValues()` reaches the
chain broadcast path, which aligns the source pass, scoped value, and inherited
consumer values before texture recreation. These paths prevent atlas
dimensions (`volumeSize` by `volumeSize^2`) and shader addressing from
disagreeing after graph load, resize, hot recompile, or a host/UI update.

`resolveDimension()` resolves `"screen"`, `"auto"`, `"input"` and
`"resolution"` to the screen size without a diagnostic; `"input"` does not
query the input texture. Any other string records `ERR_DIMENSION_FALLBACK`.

WebGL2 2D textures use nearest minification/magnification and clamp-to-edge,
except mipmapped textures (`LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` minification) and external
upload textures (linear). Its format map is `rgba8`, `rgba16f`, `rgba32f`,
`r8`, `r16f`, `r32f`, plus the WebGPU spellings `rgba8unorm`, `rgba16float`,
`rgba32float`, `r8unorm`, `r16float` and `r32float` for the same formats. Any
other string falls back to RGBA8 with an `ERR_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_FALLBACK`
diagnostic. WebGL2 3D textures use linear filtering unless the spec sets
`filter: "nearest"`, and cannot be render targets. `extractTextureSpecs()`
copies a definition's 3D `filter`, and the `Effect` config constructor keeps
`textures3d`, so the filter is authorable in both definition styles.

WebGPU maps the six WebGL spellings plus `rg8/rg16f/rg32f`, accepts listed WebGPU
spellings, and otherwise returns the provided string to WebGPU validation. The
normal surface sampler defaults to nearest for parity with WebGL2. External
uploads use the default linear sampler.

Both backends expose synchronous `updateTextureFromSource(id,source,options)`
accepting `HTMLVideoElement`, `HTMLImageElement`, `HTMLCanvasElement`, `ImageBitmap`,
or borrowed `VideoFrame`, and return `{width,height}` from the source's display or intrinsic dimensions.
For borrowed `VideoFrame` sources, both backends synchronously extract display
dimensions and submit to the GPU queue without requiring intermediate `ImageBitmap`
conversion; callers retain ownership and may close their frame synchronously immediately
after the method returns without waiting for GPU execution. WebGL2 uploads visible
pixels via `texImage2D` and rejects anamorphic display scaling (`displayWidth !== rect.width`
or `displayHeight !== rect.height`, accounting for 90°/270° rotation) returning `{width: 0, height: 0}`.
WebGPU submits `copyExternalImageToTexture()` without an awaitable completion step, handling
display scaling, rotation, crop, color, and alpha via external image copy semantics.
Unknown or zero-sized sources return zero dimensions. Canvas/media callers may
therefore read the dimensions directly on either backend rather than awaiting a
backend-specific promise.

Effects that declare an `externalTexture` (e.g. `synth/media`) bind one texture
per expanded step that consumes it, named `<externalTexture>_step_N` where `N`
is the step's node index in the compiled program (a trailing `.write()` is its
own node, so it consumes a step too). No pass ever binds the bare
`<externalTexture>` id, so hosts must upload into each step's texture and
publish the source dimensions into each step's `imageSize` uniform for the
image to render. `CanvasRenderer.getMediaSteps()` lists each media step's
texture id, pass uniform, step index, and effect from the compiled graph — the
same bindings `compileGraph()` carries as `graph.mediaSteps` — so hosts no
longer reproduce the numbering themselves; texture ids and step numbering are
unchanged for hosts that already bind `<externalTexture>_step_N`.

2D texture specs may author two opt-in allocation policies and 3D texture
specs may author a filtering policy:

- `mipmaps: true` (2D only) allocates a full mip chain
  (`floor(log2(max(w,h))) + 1` levels — WebGL2 allocates every level with
  per-level `texImage2D` calls at `createTexture()` so the texture is
  mipmap-complete before the first regeneration) and the pipeline
  regenerates it from the frame's level-0 writes after every render
  (`backend.generateMipmaps()`).
  WebGL2 blits level-1..N with a NEAREST chain; WebGPU downsamples level
  N-1 into N through cached fullscreen resample pipelines (per-level bind
  groups are cached on the texture record). Mipmapped
  textures render/compute-write into level 0 (`renderView`/single-mip
  views) and sample through the full-chain view with a linear mipmap
  sampler. Backend texture records expose `mipmaps` and `mipLevels`.
  Double-buffered global surfaces regenerate both halves each frame; for
  the read half this is idempotent (its level 0 was not written that
  frame, so the chain already matches its contents from when it was the
  write half).
- `persistent: true` (2D only) preserves contents when the texture is
  recreated at a new size (resize or parameter-driven recreation): the
  pipeline copies the old texture into a temporary, recreates at the new
  size, and resamples the temporary back through `backend.copyTexture()`
  (WebGL2 blit; WebGPU `copyTextureToTexture` when dimensions match, a
  fullscreen resample pass otherwise). Backend texture records expose
  `persistent`.
- `filter: 'nearest' | 'linear'` (3D only) selects the 3D sampling mode:
  WebGL2 sets it at `createTexture3D()` (default linear, unchanged);
  WebGPU maps it onto the shared sampler set only when authored
  (`'linear'` -> the default linear sampler; unauthored 3D sampling keeps
  the historical nearest default). Records expose `filter`.
- Unknown texture spec fields (typos) are rejected by
  `validateEffectDefinition()` with a `Texture 'x': unknown field 'y'`
  diagnostic; `filter`/`mipmaps`/`persistent` on the wrong container are
  rejected the same way. Previously accepted programs keep compiling: these
  keys were never consumed before.
- `transient` remains a non-authorable concept (absence of `persistent`).
- Implementation and focused regression coverage (validator cases,
  `extractTextureSpecs()` propagation through `compileGraph()`, pipeline
  preservation-on-resize and per-frame regeneration against recording
  backends) live in `shaders/tests/test_mip_controls.js`, wired into
  `scripts/run-js-tests.js` and `npm run test:shaders:runtime`.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `resolveDimension()`,
`clampVolumeSize()`, `clampGraphVolumeSizes()`, `applyMrtFormatBudget()`,
`setUniform()`, `broadcastChainScopedParam()`;
`shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` - `write3d`/`read3d` volume/geometry
dimension-handoff resolution (`writtenVolumes`, `readVolumes`,
`exportedTextures`, `resolveVolume()`, `resolveExport()`) and per-step
external-texture binding recording (`mediaSteps`);
`shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - `applyStepParameterValues()`;
`shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2.js` - `createTexture()`,
`createTexture3D()`, `resolveFormat()`, `probeColorBytesPerSample()`,
`updateTextureFromSource()`;
`shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgpu.js` - texture creation, samplers,
`resolveFormat()`, `updateTextureFromSource()`.

### Validate

Measurable resource predicates after `pipeline.resize(width,height)`:

```text
every resolved non-screen dimension >= 1
every graph texture has backend record with matching width and height
every 3D graph texture has matching depth and is3D === true
every global 2D surface has distinct read and write texture IDs
every pass output intended for WebGL rendering has an FBO
every format is recognized by the target backend before compilation/execution
every numeric volumeSize-family pass uniform agrees with its allocated atlas
when maxColorBytesPerSample is numeric, every MRT byte sum computed from pipeline.backend.textures is <= it; otherwise reject the graph in host policy
```

WebGL FBO completeness is checked during creation but only logged (console). WebGPU device
creation validates size/format/usage asynchronously through normal exceptions
or `uncapturederror`. Individual failures of these checks surface as structured,
non-throwing `backend.diagnostics` records (`ERR_MISSING_RENDER_TARGET`,
`ERR_GL_ERROR`, `ERR_DEVICE_VALIDATION`), but there is no public
aggregate resource-validation report.

Frame lifetime is behavior, not an authoring flag:

- Backend texture objects survive frames until resize, recompilation/recreation,
  or `dispose()`.
- WebGL passes do not clear color targets before a normal draw.
- WebGPU normal render attachments use `loadOp:"load"` unless `pass.clear`;
  authored pass-level `clear` is copied onto the expanded pass and reaches
  this loadOp.
- Global surfaces are double-buffered. Display surfaces swap at frame end.
  Names classified as state (`xyz`, `vel`, `rgba`, `trail`, suffix variants,
  names containing `state`, scoped particle state) preserve final frame-local
  bindings.
- A node-local texture can therefore retain data across frames. With the
  opt-in `persistent` texture-spec policy, a recreated
  allocation also preserves its previous contents across size changes, and
  backend texture records expose the `persistent` and `mipmaps`/`mipLevels`
  class flags for query.

Sources: backend texture/FBO creation; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` -
`swapBuffers()`, `resize()`, `dispose()`.

### Diagnose

Resource failures include:

```text
WebGL Error: Texture <textureId> not found                 (raw Error in readPixels)
WebGPU: {code:"ERR_TEXTURE_NOT_FOUND", pass, texture}
WebGL console: FBO incomplete for texture <id>: <status>
WebGL console: MRT FBO incomplete for <id>: <status>
WebGL console: [executePass] FBO not found for <id> in pass <pass>
[Pipeline] Capping volumeSize from <requested> to <effective>: the <requested>x<requested-squared> volume atlas exceeds this device's max texture size (<limit>)
[Pipeline] Demoting MRT attachment <id> from <format> to rgba16f: pass <pass> needs <bytes> bytes/sample, device allows <budget>
WebGPU console: Storage texture <id> not found
WebGPU uncaptured error: <device validation message>
```

WebGL unknown formats silently become RGBA8. WebGPU unknown formats reach device
validation. Unknown dimension forms resolve to screen size. Neither fallback
rejects previously accepted input, and both now surface structured,
deduplicated diagnostics instead of silence: WebGL unknown
formats emit a once-per-format `[WebGL2]` warning plus a queryable
`ERR_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_FALLBACK` record in `backend.diagnostics`, and unknown
dimension forms emit a once-per-spec `[Pipeline]` warning plus a queryable
`ERR_DIMENSION_FALLBACK` record in `pipeline.diagnostics`. Unknown texture spec fields and
misplaced `filter`/`mipmaps`/`persistent` keys are rejected by
`validateEffectDefinition()`.

After MRT adaptation, inspect the backend texture records. The pipeline
recreates an allocation when its recorded format does not match the graph.
FBO/GL diagnostics keep their console messages and additionally record
structured `backend.diagnostics` entries (`ERR_MISSING_RENDER_TARGET`,
`ERR_GL_ERROR`).

WebGL per-pass and presentation `gl.getError()` logging is armed only for the
first three frames after a program compile or 2D texture allocation. It is
disabled in steady state to avoid a synchronous CPU/GPU round trip. Late GL
errors are therefore not surfaced by those per-frame checks. FBO completeness
checks still run when render targets are created.

The WebGL MRT budget probe restores the default framebuffer.
It deletes its temporary textures/framebuffer and drains errors from rejected probe combinations.
This prevents later pass checks from attributing those errors to the wrong operation.

Sources: backend texture and pass execution methods, including WebGL
`probeColorBytesPerSample()`; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` -
`resolveDimension()`, `clampVolumeSize()`, `createSurfaces()`, and
`recreateTextures()`.

<!-- SURFACE:MUTATION -->
## Compatibility and mutation

### Introspect

Compile the DSL. Then call `listSteps(compiled)`:

```ts
type StepInfo = {
  stepIndex: number
  planIndex: number
  chainIndex: number
  effectName: string
  isStarter: boolean
  isStarterPosition: boolean
  canReplaceWithStarter: boolean
  canReplaceWithNonStarter: boolean
  args: Record<string, unknown>
}
```

`stepIndex` is the compiled effect step's `temp`. Branch objects do not have
`chain` and are skipped by these mutation helpers. Compiled nodes marked
`builtin: true`, including `read`, `write`, 3D I/O, and subchain boundaries,
are also excluded. A two-effect chain ending in `.write(o0)` therefore returns
two entries while retaining the effects' original step and chain indexes.
`getCompatibleReplacements()` enumerates the currently registered `ops` and
partitions them by starter state.

Sources: `shaders/src/lang/transform.js` - `listSteps()`,
`getCompatibleReplacements()`, `predictReplacement()`; `shaders/src/lang/ops.js` - `ops`;
`shaders/src/lang/paramAliases.js` - `getParamAliases()`;
`shaders/tests/test_transform.js` - effect-only length, index, and builtin-target
regressions.

### Act

```ts
type ReplacementQuery =
  | { success: true, compatible: string[], incompatible: string[],
      predictions: Record<string, ReplacementPrediction>,
      blocked?: { effect: string, issues: ReplacementPredictionIssue[] }[] }
  | { success: false, error: string }

type ReplacementResult =
  | { success: true, program: CompiledProgram, prediction: ReplacementPrediction }
  | { success: false, error: string, prediction?: ReplacementPrediction }

getCompatibleReplacements(
  compiled: CompiledProgram,
  stepIndex: number,
  options?: { searchOrder?: string[], preflight?: boolean, manifest?: object }
): ReplacementQuery

replaceEffect(
  compiled: CompiledProgram,
  stepIndex: number,
  newEffectName: string,
  newArgs?: Record<string, unknown>,
  options?: { searchOrder?: string[], preflight?: boolean, manifest?: object }
): ReplacementResult
```

Every successful listing attaches `predictions`: a per-candidate prediction
(`predictReplacement()` in `shaders/src/lang/transform.js`) of the candidate's
compatibility dimensions — shader availability (registered definition in the
runtime registry; `available` is `unknown` when no definitions are registered
at all), arguments (unknown names, with param-alias awareness via the read-only
`getParamAliases()` in `shaders/src/lang/paramAliases.js`, and missing
no-default arguments), types, ranges (min/max/choices, reported under the
canonical argument name), passes, outputs, sampler topology (with the replaced
effect's topology as `changedFrom`), and backend support from the optional
`options.manifest` (`effects/manifest.json` shape). Dimensions without
available data are reported as `unknown`, never invented. Listing-time
predictions use empty arguments, so requires-arguments candidates are not
blocked, and missing no-default arguments are informative rather than hard
issues. With the explicit `preflight: true` opt-in, candidates whose
prediction found hard issues (availability, unknown arguments, type
mismatches, range/choice violations) move out of `compatible` into `blocked`
with the reasons; the default classification is otherwise unchanged, so
previously accepted input is only rejected behind the opt-in. `replaceEffect`
attaches the same prediction to every success as `prediction`, and with
`preflight: true` it refuses mutation when the prediction finds hard issues,
returning `success: false` with `error: "Replacement preflight failed: ..."`
plus the prediction.

The checkable current definition of compatible is exactly:

```text
target effect exists in ops
AND
isStarterPosition(step) === isStarterOp(target effect)
```

where `isStarterPosition(step)` is:

```text
chainIndex === 0
OR (isStarterOp(step.op) AND (step.from === null OR step.from === undefined))
```

A step is in starter position if it is either (a) the first step in the chain
(`chainIndex === 0`), or (b) an inline surface producer — a registered starter
effect with no pipeline predecessor (`from === null/undefined`) that the compiler
flattened into the chain as a dependency of a surface-type parameter (e.g.
`heightTex: noise()`).

No other shape participates. `replaceEffect` performs these steps:

1. Deep-clone the compiled program.
2. Start with every target argument default.
3. Apply `newArgs` over those defaults.
4. Round non-integer numeric `newArgs` to three decimal places.
5. Run `predictReplacement()`. With `options.preflight === true` and any
   issue, return `{ success: false, error: "Replacement preflight failed:
   ...", prediction }` without mutating.
6. Add the namespace to `searchNamespaces` if needed.
7. Set the resolved operator name and arguments.
8. Reset namespace metadata.

Sources: `shaders/src/lang/transform.js` - `replaceEffect()`,
`predictReplacement()`; `shaders/src/lang/paramAliases.js` - `getParamAliases()`.

### Validate

Mutation succeeds only when `result.success === true`. That proves effect
existence and starter-position compatibility. It does **not** prove the mutated
program compiles or renders. A complete falsifiable gate is:

```text
replacement.success === true
AND unparse(replacement.program) parses
AND semantic_error_count === 0
AND expansion_error_count === 0
AND both required backend compilers succeed
AND rendered-output thresholds pass
AND parity status is ok when required
```

`getCompatibleReplacements().compatible` is therefore a candidate list, not a
swappability guarantee. The additive `predictions` field (and, behind the
`preflight: true` opt-in, `blocked` with reasons) reports the predicted
compatibility dimensions per candidate, but only a real compile/render/parity
run proves an end-to-end replacement.

Sources: `shaders/tests/test_transform.js`; compiler, render, and parity
contracts in this document.

### Diagnose

Enumerated mutation rejection strings are:

```text
Invalid compiled program: missing plans
Step with index <stepIndex> not found
Effect '<newEffectName>' not found
Cannot replace starter effect '<old>' with non-starter effect '<new>'. The first effect in a chain must be a starting effect.
Cannot replace non-starter effect '<old>' with starter effect '<new>'. Starting effects can only appear at the beginning of a chain.
Replacement preflight failed: <predicted issue messages joined by '; '>
```

After a successful replacement, all parse, semantic, expansion, backend, output,
and parity failures use their respective surfaces' diagnostic channels.
Parameter names/types/ranges, pass shape, shader availability, and backend
support are predicted before mutation by `predictReplacement()`. Availability,
arguments (param-alias aware), types and ranges raise issues that can block;
passes, outputs and sampler topology are reported for information and never
block; backend support is predicted only when the
caller supplies `options.manifest`; dimensions without data are reported
`unknown`, never invented. The `preflight: true` opt-in turns hard issues into
rejection; without it the prediction is returned and mutation is unchanged.

Builtin step indexes use the same `Step with index <stepIndex> not found`
failure as other non-target indexes. Callers do not need to parse builtin names
because builtin nodes are absent from `listSteps()` and cannot be resolved by
either mutation helper.

Sources: `shaders/src/lang/transform.js` - all `success:false` paths.

<!-- SURFACE:OUTPUT -->
## Rendered output

### Introspect

`renderEffectFrame` reads the render surface through `backend.readPixels()` on
both backends, after draining submitted work, and falls back to the WebGL
default framebuffer (the presented canvas) only when no surface is readable.
For a timed capture it redraws at the requested paused time. The decoded
success payload is:

```ts
type ImageMetrics = {
  mean_rgb: Vec3                 // each component in [0,1]
  mean_alpha: number             // [0,1]
  std_rgb: Vec3                  // each population stddev in [0,0.5]
  luma_variance: number          // population variance in [0,0.25]
  unique_sampled_colors: number  // integer in [1,sample_count]
  is_all_zero: boolean
  is_all_transparent: boolean
  is_essentially_blank: boolean
  is_monochrome: boolean
}

type RenderSuccess = {
  effect_id: string
  status: "ok"
  backend: string
  requested_resolution?: [number, number]
  warning?: string              // present when frame size differs from request
  frame: { image_uri: string | null, width: number, height: number }
  metrics: ImageMetrics
  console_errors?: string[]
}

type RenderFailure = {
  effect_id?: string
  status: "error"
  backend?: "unknown" | string
  requested_resolution?: [number, number]
  error: string
  console_errors?: string[]
}
```

The sample stride is
`max(1,floor(width*height/1000))`. Every `stride`th pixel is sampled. Therefore
sample count is `ceil(width*height/stride)` and can exceed 1000 (for the worked
256x256 capture it is 1009). Colors are exact 8-bit RGB triplets. Alpha is not
part of color cardinality.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts` -
`renderEffectFrame()`; `src/harness/types.ts` - `ImageMetrics`, `RenderResult`.

The engine-native output path exposes sinks and bounded asynchronous frame
export independently of Shade MCP:

```ts
type SinkDescriptor = {
  width: number
  height: number
  format: "rgba8unorm"
  colorSpace: "srgb" | "display-p3"
  alphaMode: "opaque" | "straight" | "premultiplied"
  fps: number                      // finite and > 0
}

type PackedFrame = {
  width: number
  height: number
  rowStride: number                // width * 4, with no row padding
  data: Uint8Array                 // top-down packed RGBA8 rows
}

type Sink = {
  configure(descriptor: SinkDescriptor): unknown
  submit(textureId: string, presentationTimestamp: number): boolean | unknown
  close(options?: { backendLost?: boolean }): unknown
  deferRender?(): boolean
}

type SinkStats = { accepted: number, dropped: number, failed: number }
type FrameExportStats = {
  accepted: number
  dropped: number
  completed: number
  failed: number
}
```

`Pipeline.sinkManager.stats` is a `Map<Sink,SinkStats>` for active sinks.
`FrameExportQueue.stats` is one stable mutable `FrameExportStats` object, and
`queue.available` is true exactly when the queue is configured, open, and has a
free slot. `CanvasSink`, `SinkManager`, and `FrameExportQueue` are exported from
`shaders/src/index.js`.

The generic sink boundary does not validate descriptors: `Pipeline.resize()`
forwards its `width` and `height` arguments, and `SinkManager.configure()`
stores and broadcasts the supplied value. When a `FrameExportQueue` uses the WebGL2 or WebGPU adapter, slot creation requires `width` and `height` to be positive safe integers.
The format, color-space, alpha-mode, and fps predicates shown above must also hold.

Sources: `shaders/src/runtime/sink.js`; `shaders/src/runtime/frame-export.js`;
`shaders/src/index.js`.

### Act

Call the MCP verb documented in the tool section. For deterministic MCP
captures, supply `time`. With an explicit `time`, the released verb
(`src/tools/browser/render.ts` at the pinned snapshot) awaits its frame-count
warmup while the render loop is still live, bounds both render and DSL warmup
waits at `session.timeoutMs` with a diagnostic, unpauses in a `finally`, and
after the pause redraws explicitly at the requested paused time before the
readback — the same value handed to `setPausedTime`, which is what a paused
single-frame render draws. A time-less request keeps the historical
live-frame readback (the last frame the running loop drew), which is
nondeterministic with the capture moment; a timed request reproduces
byte-identically per requested time. The repository harness
(`shaders/tests/test-harness.js`) renders through this verb on both backends
and adds its temporal metrics to the result.

For direct rendering, use `CanvasRenderer`/`Pipeline`.
Then read `pipeline.getOutput()` with backend readback.

Uniform override keys are shader uniform names as consumed by
`pipeline.setUniform`, not necessarily DSL global names. `resolution` sets the
browser viewport and calls the renderer's `resize(width, height)`, which sets
the pipeline's render size; the viewer's layout still sizes the presented
canvas. The returned frame is read from the render surface, so the worked call
requesting 256x256 captures 256x256 although the demo viewer presents it in a
90x90 canvas.
`CanvasRenderer` sizes an unsized canvas element (no width/height attributes)
from its `width`/`height` options at construction; an element sized by
attribute or property keeps that size, and a disagreement with the renderer
options emits exactly one diagnostic naming both sizes. `resize()` changes the
render resolution but not the canvas element, so a host that requests a
different capture resolution must resize the element itself.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts` - request handling;
Noisemaker `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - construction-time element
sizing, `resize()`; Noisemaker `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` -
`setUniform()`, `getOutput()`.

For engine-native delivery, compile first.
Then register a sink on that concrete pipeline:

```ts
const queue = renderer.createFrameExportQueue({
  slots: 3,
  onError(error) { report(error) }
})

const remove = renderer.addSink({
  configure(descriptor) { queue.configure(descriptor) },
  submit(textureId, timestamp) {
    return queue.enqueue(textureId, timestamp, consumeFrame)
  },
  close(options) { queue.close(options) }
})

function serviceExports() {
  queue.poll()
  requestAnimationFrame(serviceExports)
}
serviceExports()
```

`CanvasRenderer.addSink()` and `createFrameExportQueue()` throw before a
pipeline exists. `addSink()` returns an idempotent removal function scoped to
the current pipeline. Removing it closes that sink once. Sinks are not migrated
when recompilation replaces a pipeline.

`createFrameExportQueue()` returns null
when the active backend does not implement export. WebGL2 and WebGPU both do.
The base `Backend` does not.

`FrameExportQueue` is not itself a `Sink`: it has `configure()`, `enqueue()`,
`poll()`, and `close()`, so a host supplies the small adapter above. The queue
owns three slots by default. `slots` must be an integer from 2 through 8.

`configure()` preallocates every slot. `enqueue(textureId,timestamp,onFrame,
context?)` starts work only when a slot is free and returns a boolean. The host
must call `poll()`. There is no internal timer. A successful callback receives
`(frame,timestamp,context)` with the latter two values unchanged.

Pipeline resize configures all current sinks with exactly
`{width,height,format:"rgba8unorm",colorSpace:"srgb",
alphaMode:"premultiplied",fps:60}`. A sink added after resize is configured
immediately with the same descriptor. Sinks may implement an optional
`deferRender(): boolean` method: while any active sink returns `true`,
`Pipeline.shouldDeferRender()` returns `true` and the host render loop
(`CanvasRenderer._renderLoop`) skips drawing the current tick while holding canvas
contents and advancing animation time, incrementing `CanvasRenderer.deferredFrameCount`.
Sinks without `deferRender()` never defer rendering. Rendering submits the selected
pre-swap texture ID and the caller's presentation timestamp, or `performance.now()`
with a `Date.now()` fallback. A graph with no render surface advances the frame
without submitting to sinks.

Both backend queues produce top-down, tightly packed RGBA8. WebGL2 resolves to
an RGBA8 texture, flips vertically in the resolve shader, reads into a pixel
pack buffer, and polls a fence with zero timeout. WebGPU resolves to
`rgba8unorm` (inverting vertical orientation in the resolve shader to match
canvas presentation), copies into 256-byte-aligned staging rows, maps
asynchronously, and removes row padding before delivery. `straight` preserves
RGBA, `opaque` forces alpha to one, and `premultiplied` multiplies RGB by
alpha. `colorSpace` and `fps` are validated descriptor metadata. Neither backend
adapter performs a color-space conversion or frame-rate throttle.

Each slot reuses one `PackedFrame` object and `Uint8Array`. A callback that
retains a frame past later deliveries on the same slot must copy its data.

Sources: `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - `addSink()`, `deferredFrameCount`,
`createFrameExportQueue()`; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `resize()`,
`render()`, `shouldDeferRender()`; `shaders/src/runtime/sink.js` -
`shouldDeferRender()`; `shaders/src/runtime/frame-export.js`;
`shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2-frame-export.js`;
`shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgpu-frame-export.js`.

### Validate

The implemented predicates are exactly:

```text
is_all_zero         = every sample has r, g and b <= 0.001
is_all_transparent  = every sample has alpha <= 0.001
is_essentially_blank= luma_variance < 0.0001
is_monochrome       = unique_sampled_colors <= 1   // exact 8-bit RGB triples
```

For an ordinary non-exempt effect, the repository harness requires:

```text
status === "ok"
is_all_transparent === false
is_essentially_blank === false
is_monochrome === false
no console error, warning, or page error   // two known-benign messages are ignored under CI
```

`is_essentially_blank` means low spatial luma variance, not black. A constant
white image satisfies it. The harness exemptions are:

- monochrome: `filter/a`, `filter/shape`, `filter/solid`, `synth/solid`.
- low-luma-variance: `synth/solid`.
- transparency: none.

There is no implemented no-animation pass threshold and no default
low-variety gate. The harness `renderEffectFrame` wrapper
(`shaders/tests/test-harness.js`) additionally returns three additive
metrics on every successful frame: `temporal_diff` (normalized mean
absolute RGB difference between two renders at normalized times 0 and 0.5,
so a looping effect cannot alias to "static" through phase alignment),
`is_no_animation` = `temporal_diff <= 0.01`, and `is_low_variety` =
`unique_sampled_colors <= 5`. These are repository-local diagnostic
thresholds; Shade MCP's filter modification tool now uses a different
output-to-input pixel comparison. The probe is an external two-frame
comparison; if pixel readback
fails, the three metrics are `null` and `metrics.temporal_probe_error`
names the failure. The harness exposes an explicit opt-in `--low-variety`
gate with exemptions `filter/shape`, `filter/solid`, and `synth/solid`; the
default run applies no low-variety or no-animation rejection, and static
output is deliberately never gated (legitimate for many effects).
Regressions: `shaders/tests/test_frame_metrics.js`, registered in
`scripts/run-js-tests.js`. These metrics are returned by this repository's
harness wrapper, not by the upstream Shade MCP verb.

The separate filter modification tool compares the rendered output with its
consumed input at one paused time. It passes only when normalized mean
absolute RGB difference exceeds `0.01`; this is not an animation or color-
variety validator.

The repository sustained benchmark gate uses median frame time after 20 warmup
frames and 100 measured frames and fails when `fps < 30`. Equivalently it passes
when `fps >= 30`. The MCP benchmark instead passes when
`fps >= target_fps`, where the default target is 60.

For a `SinkManager`, `submit() === true` increments `accepted`, false increments
`dropped`, and a thrown submit, broadcast-`configure()`, or `deferRender()` error increments
`failed`. Thrown errors in `deferRender()` are isolated and do not defer rendering;
if `onError` was supplied it is invoked with `(error, sink)`. Other return values change
no counter. One failing registered sink does not stop later sinks. Adding a sink after
the manager is configured calls that sink's `configure()` before registration. If it throws,
`add()` propagates the error and creates no stats record. For the pipeline's default
manager there is no `onError` callback, so inspect its stats when an external sink can throw.

For a `FrameExportQueue`, a successful adapter `begin()` increments `accepted`.
Unconfigured, closed, or full-queue enqueue attempts increment `dropped` and
return false. Begin, poll, read, and callback failures increment `failed` and
invoke `onError` when supplied. A callback increments `completed` only after it
returns normally. A failed slot is released for reuse. Descriptor validation
and slot allocation failures from `configure()` throw synchronously.

When reconfiguration or close destroys a pending slot, the queue increments
`dropped` before clearing its callback and context. This also applies to
backend-loss close, without attempting GPU destruction. Completed and failed
records are already released and are not counted again. A host that separately
tracks enqueue results and pending callbacks can use the increment to reconcile
outstanding frames after the lifecycle call. `dropped` also includes enqueue
attempts rejected before acceptance, so stats alone do not identify which
accepted frame was canceled.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts`, `passthrough.ts`,
`benchmark.ts`; `shaders/tests/test-harness.js` - metric gates, exemptions, and
sustained benchmark; `shaders/src/runtime/sink.js`;
`shaders/src/runtime/frame-export.js`.

### Diagnose

In-page render failures include:

```text
No renderer
No renderer on <backend>
Failed to read pixels on <backend>: no readable render surface
```

Outer browser/session failures use `{effect_id,status:"error",error:string}`.
Captured console messages can appear as `console_errors`, but backend console
diagnostics are strings rather than typed error objects.

The delivered `renderEffectFrame` reads pixels through `backend.readPixels()`
on both backends and drains the WebGPU command queue before reading. It reads
the half of the render surface's ping-pong pair that the last frame presented
(`pipeline.frameReadTextures`), then `global_<surface>_read`, then the last
node output, so the frame size is the pipeline's render size, not the size
of the viewer's presented canvas. The repository harness uses this verb on
both backends.
When `resolution` is requested, the verb echoes `requested_resolution` and
includes a `warning` with requested and actual dimensions if the viewer did
not honor it. The returned frame dimensions are authoritative.

`renderEffectFrame`, `runDslProgram`, and the vendored library helper
`computeImageMetrics` share one implementation: the verb reads the frame back
in screen order and computes its metrics in Node with `computeImageMetrics`.
Each `ImageMetrics` field therefore has one definition across verbs and the
library export.

Sink validation rejects anything without callable `configure`, `submit`, and
`close` methods. A closed manager rejects new sinks, duplicate registration is
an error, and removing a sink closes it. Manager close attempts every active
sink, then throws the first close error after clearing all registrations.
Pipeline disposal closes sinks before backend resources. `backendLost:true`
propagates to sink close so a frame queue abandons unsafe GPU resources without
calling its adapter. Normal close destroys each slot.

Frame-export failures are ordinary `TypeError`, `RangeError`, or `Error`
objects, not a shared code union. Stable validation messages include:

```text
Sink must implement configure, submit, and close
Frame export adapter must implement createSlot, begin, poll, read, and destroySlot
Frame export slots must be an integer from 2 through 8
Frame export callback must be a function
Frame export width must be a positive integer
Frame export height must be a positive integer
WebGL2 frame export format must be 'rgba8unorm'
WebGPU frame export format must be 'rgba8unorm'
WebGL2 frame export colorSpace must be 'srgb' or 'display-p3'
WebGPU frame export colorSpace must be 'srgb' or 'display-p3'
WebGL2 frame export alphaMode must be 'opaque', 'straight', or 'premultiplied'
WebGPU frame export alphaMode must be 'opaque', 'straight', or 'premultiplied'
Frame export fps must be finite and positive
```

Adapters additionally report missing textures, source/configured extent
mismatches, unusable or wrongly sequenced slots, allocation/compile/link/fence
failures, unavailable WebGPU constants, and map failures. Queue `onError`
receives those objects but no texture ID, timestamp, slot index, or normalized
phase field. On reconfigure/close, accepted pending frames suppress their
callbacks and increment `dropped` once before their records are released.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts`; `src/harness/pixel-reader.ts` -
`computeImageMetrics()`; `shaders/tests/test-harness.js` -
WebGPU render wrapper; `shaders/src/runtime/sink.js`;
`shaders/src/runtime/frame-export.js`; backend frame-export adapters.

<!-- SURFACE:PARITY -->
## Cross-backend parity

### Introspect

Before rendering, inspect the manifest and `checkEffectStructure`:

- every referenced program must have a GLSL `.glsl` or `.vert`/`.frag` entry.
- every referenced program must have a same-stem WGSL `.wgsl` entry.
- `structuralParityIssues` must be empty.
- `compareShaders` exposes line counts, detected functions, and detected uniform
  declarations, but does not establish semantic equivalence.
- `checkAlgEquiv` is an optional AI judgment, not a numeric parity signal.

Backend authorability from current source:

| Feature | WebGL2 authoring | WebGPU authoring | Predictable parity status |
|---|---|---|---|
| fullscreen fragment | GLSL ES 3 combined fragment or split vertex/fragment | WGSL fragment, optional WGSL vertex | authorable when both sources/bindings implement same math |
| MRT | multiple fragment outputs. Queried draw-buffer limit and probed combined-byte budget | multiple `@location` outputs/attachments. Device byte limit | pipeline can demote trailing full-float outputs. Reuse validates the allocated format. Parity still requires inspecting allocated backend formats on both devices |
| points/billboards/triangles | draw modes supported | draw modes supported | authorable. Coordinate/winding conventions still require pixel test |
| compile-time define | GLSL `#define` | typed WGSL module `const` | authorable for boolean/numeric compatible uses |
| native compute | absent | compute-only WGSL selected from `@compute` | impossible as native parity |
| compute-style fallback | hand-authored GLSL fragment plus `storageTextures`/output mapping | native compute/storage | only authorable when the GLSL fragment explicitly reproduces the algorithm. No translation exists |
| storage buffers | no equivalent binding path | parsed/bound by WebGPU | generally impossible parity without a different GLSL algorithm |
| 3D sampling | supported | supported | authorable |
| rendering directly to 3D texture | explicitly unsupported | storage/render workflows available | impossible direct parity. Use a 2D atlas/common algorithm |

There is now a single capability-preflight API that consumes a definition and
returns this determination: `preflightEffect(definition, capabilities,
shaders)` in `shaders/src/runtime/preflight.js` reports per-backend
authorability (`backends.webgl2`/`backends.webgpu` with `authorable` and
`reasons`; each backend's source is selected in that backend's own order —
WebGL2 `source`, `glsl`, `fragment`; WebGPU `wgsl`, `source`, non-GLSL
`fragment` — and must be in that backend's language), the
predicted MRT attachment demotions `applyMrtFormatBudget()` will perform
(`formatChanges`, trailing rgba32f → rgba16f under
`maxColorBytesPerSample`), and predicted `maxTextureSize` clamps
(`clamps`). Without shader source information the source checks are
skipped, so `authorable` reflects only the structural and limit checks.
`Pipeline.preflight()`
consumes the pipeline's own graph and capabilities.

For a reused pipeline, parity checks must read each allocated backend texture's
effective format. Do not use only the adapted graph specification as evidence.

Sources: `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - `loadEffectShaders()`;
backend `compileProgram()`, `executePass()`, `createTexture3D()`;
Shade MCP analysis tools.

### Act

Author shader programs with the same filename stem.
Keep binding names/types aligned with the expanded pass. WebGL `compileProgram()` accepts `spec.source`, `spec.glsl`, or
`spec.fragment`, plus optional `spec.vertex`. As of noisemaker `ff1bfbc1`,
`spec.defines` is injected as `#define`s into a custom `spec.vertex` whenever
one is present and `spec.defines` is non-empty, the same way it already was
into the fragment stage; before that fix a custom vertex shader referencing a
`defines`-only identifier (for example a per-pass `defines`-selected constant
from `PassSpec.defines`, see Passes and render graph) would fail to compile
with an undeclared-identifier error. WebGPU selects `spec.wgsl`, then
`source` (whatever its language; GLSL there fails at WGSL compilation), then a
`fragment` without `#version`. WebGPU detects entry points
from annotations and uses `entryPoint`/specific entry-point fields where
provided.

Pixel parity request:

```ts
testPixelParity({
  effect_id?: string,
  effects?: string,  // CSV, not expanded glob syntax
  epsilon?: number,  // default 1; no runtime range validation
  seed?: number      // default 42
})
```

The tool performs these steps:

1. Select WebGL2.
2. Wait for a post-selection graph for the requested effect and backend.
3. Render six live frames for warmup.
4. Capture the offscreen render surface at time zero.
5. Select WebGPU.
6. Repeat steps 2-4.

The tool writes the seed to pipeline/pass uniforms. WebGPU rows are vertically
flipped to the same top-down orientation as WebGL before comparison.

`setBackend()` rejects a switch that fails to reach the requested backend.
Each parity leg selects the effect and waits for a graph built after that
selection, with the page-confirmed effect identity and backend checked before
capture. A failed leg returns an error identifying the leg and observed page
state. The result reports the confirmed identity of the final WebGPU leg.
The tool's browser session launches on the WebGL2 launch path, so where that
browser cannot obtain a Vulkan-backed WebGPU adapter — a GPU-less container
without a system Vulkan driver, for instance — the WebGPU leg's rebuild falls
back to WebGL2 and the leg fails closed with the page-confirmed mismatch
(`WebGPU leg: The viewer is rendering on WebGL2, not the requested webgpu`)
instead of comparing a fallback frame; the comparison itself is unchanged
where a WebGPU-flagged browser session runs the same legs.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - `testPixelParity()`,
`warmUp()`, `captureSurface()`; Shade MCP
`src/harness/browser-session.ts` - `selectEffect()`; Noisemaker
`demo/shaders/index.html` - `selectEffect()`.

### Validate

For RGBA8 channel arrays of equal dimensions:

```text
channel_diff       = abs(webgl_channel - webgpu_channel)        // [0,255]
channel_mismatch   = channel_diff > epsilon
max_diff           = max(channel_diff)                           // [0,255]
mean_diff          = sum(channel_diff) / channel_count           // [0,255]
mismatch_count     = count(channel_mismatch)                      // [0,channel_count]
mismatch_percent   = 100 * mismatch_count / channel_count        // [0,100]
status             = "ok" iff mismatch_percent < 1
```

The required literal contract marker is `mismatch_percent < 1`.

Solid-color diagnostics compute raw 0-255 RGB population variance for each
backend. A backend is solid when all three variances are `< 5`. Variances and
means are rounded to integer arrays in output. The predicate uses unrounded
values.

Y-flip diagnostics compare normal mean absolute difference with a vertically
flipped WebGPU comparison:

```text
y_flip_ratio = y_flip_mean_diff / mean_diff, or 1 when mean_diff === 0
y_flip_detected = mean_diff > 2
                  && y_flip_mean_diff < mean_diff
                  && y_flip_ratio < 0.7
y_flip_clean_flip = mean_diff > 2 && y_flip_ratio < 0.25
```

`epsilon` is described as 0-255 but Zod does not enforce that range. A strict
caller must require `0 <= epsilon <= 255` and a finite value before calling.

These predicates validate the two captured buffers. Successful captures also
require a confirmed backend switch and requested-effect graph for each leg;
check the returned final-leg `effect_id` and `backend` before accepting the
numeric verdict.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - comparison, solid, and
Y-flip predicates.

### Diagnose

```ts
type ParitySuccessOrMismatch = {
  effect_id: string
  backend?: string
  status: "ok" | "mismatch"
  maxDiff: number
  meanDiff: number
  mismatchCount: number
  mismatchPercent: number
  resolution: [number, number]
  glslSolid: boolean
  wgslSolid: boolean
  glslVariance: [number, number, number]
  wgslVariance: [number, number, number]
  yFlipDetected: boolean
  yFlipCleanFlip: boolean
  yFlipMismatchPercent: number
  yFlipMeanDiff: number
  yFlipRatio: number
  issues: string[]
  details: string
  console_errors?: string[]
}

type ParityFailure = {
  effect_id?: string
  status: "error"
  maxDiff?: 0
  meanDiff?: 0
  mismatchCount?: 0
  mismatchPercent?: 0
  resolution?: [number, number]
  details?: string
  error?: string
  console_errors?: string[]
}
```

Enumerated in-tool error details are `WebGL2 leg: Failed to capture WebGL2`,
`WebGPU leg: Failed to capture WebGPU`, and
`Capture size mismatch: glsl <w>x<h> vs wgsl <w>x<h>`. Compile/browser failures
can instead use the outer `{effect_id,status:"error",error}` shape.

Issues include `GLSL SOLID COLOR (mean=...)`, `WGSL SOLID COLOR (mean=...)`, and
`Y-FLIP`/`PARTIAL Y-FLIP DETECTED (...)`. Solid-color and Y-flip issues do not
change `status`. Status depends only on mismatch percentage. A strict gate must
also assert both solid flags false and `yFlipDetected === false` unless the
effect is intentionally solid.

Selection failures, backend-switch failures, and identity mismatches return
`status:"error"` with the failed leg in `details` and the page-confirmed
effect/backend when available. They do not produce a numeric parity success.

Backend compilation failures:

```ts
// Shared pipeline
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_SPEC_MISSING", program: string, pass: string }

// WebGL2
ShaderDiagnostic { code: "ERR_SHADER_MISSING", backend: "webgl2", stage: "missing-source",
  program: string, detail: "Shader source missing for program '<id>'. You may need to regenerate the shader manifest." }
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_COMPILE", detail: string, source: string }
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_LINK", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_UNIFORM_BLOCK_TOO_LARGE", detail: string, program: WebGLProgram }
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_TOO_MANY_TEXTURES", pass: string, limit: number }

// WebGPU
{ code: "ERR_NO_WGSL_SOURCE", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_COMPILE", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_TEXTURE_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, texture: string }
{ code: "ERR_NO_MRT_OUTPUTS", pass: string }
{ code: "ERR_COMPUTE_DISPATCH_UNRESOLVED", pass: string, detail: string }
```

Sources: backend compile/execute methods; Shade MCP
`src/tools/browser/parity.ts`.

<!-- SURFACE:MCP -->
## Shade MCP tool contracts

### Introspect

1. Call MCP `initialize`.
2. Send `notifications/initialized`.
3. Call `tools/list`.

For the snapshot at the top of this document, `tools/list` returned the 18 verb
names documented below. Every tool descriptor declares
`inputSchema.$schema:"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"` and
`execution:{taskSupport:"forbidden"}`. None declares an `outputSchema`.
`renderEffectFrame.uniforms` and `runDslProgram.uniforms` are object schemas
with string `propertyNames` and numeric `additionalProperties`. The Zod 4
upgrade did not change their `Record<string,number>` application contract.

The 0.4.x releases keep accepted argument types and defaults and change result
schemas: every result carries `outcome` and multi-effect results use the
batch envelope (below); `definition.js` projections can carry `partial` and
`partialReasons`; `checkEffectStructure` can report `unusedFilesUnchecked`;
`ImageMetrics` has one definition for every verb; `testUniformResponsiveness`
reports an unresponsive uniform as `fail`; and the capture verbs read the
presented half of the render surface. Knowledge-search results are source
guidance, not a rendered-loop validation result.

The transport result for every verb is:

```ts
type McpTextResult = {
  content: [{ type: "text", text: string /* JSON envelope */ },
            ...Array<{ type: "image", data: string, mimeType: "image/png" }>]
  isError?: true
}

type Outcome = "ok" | "fail" | "warning" | "skipped" | "error"
```

Decode `JSON.parse(result.content.find(x => x.type === "text").text)` before
applying the payload types below. Every text payload is JSON, including errors
thrown before a handler's own error handling, which arrive as
`{ outcome: "error", status: "error", error: string }`. The exception is an
argument that fails a tool's input schema: the MCP SDK rejects it before the
tool runs, as plain text (`MCP error -32602: Input validation error: ...`)
with `isError:true`. Every single result carries a top-level `outcome`,
computed from the tool's own `status`: `fail` for a negative verdict (parity
`mismatch`, `passthrough`, `divergent`, a uniform `fail`, `meets_target:
false`), `warning` for findings to review, `skipped` when nothing was
testable, `error` when no verdict was produced (or, for a payload with no
`status`, when it carries an `error` string), otherwise `ok`. An `outcome`
key inside the payload never overrides it. Verb-specific fields stay beside
it. `isError:true` marks a whole-call failure: a single `error` result, or a
batch in which every entry is an `error`. These tools do not declare MCP
structured content/output schemas.

The repository config supplies:

```text
SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR=./shaders/effects
SHADE_VIEWER_ROOT=.
SHADE_VIEWER_PATH=/demo/shaders/
SHADE_GLOBALS_PREFIX=__noisemaker
```

The package requires Node 22 or newer. Browser sessions are headless unless
`SHADE_HEADLESS` is `0` or `false`. `SHADE_SWIFTSHADER=1` or `true` opts into
Chromium's software rasterizer.

`SHADE_TIMEOUT_MS` supplies the session default
for Playwright operations that honor it and is also used explicitly by backend,
status, and graph readiness polls. The parity six-frame warmup instead retains
an explicit `30000` ms bound.

`SHADE_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds AI provider requests. Both configurable timeouts
are parsed with `parseInt(value, 10)` and default to `120000` ms when that result
is non-finite or nonpositive. Fractional text is truncated and a numeric prefix
followed by nonnumeric text is accepted.

`SHADE_AI_MODEL` overrides the provider model. Without an override, Anthropic
uses `claude-opus-5` and OpenAI uses `gpt-5.2`. SIGINT and SIGTERM close live
browser sessions and the shared viewer server before process exit.

The advertised MCP server version is injected from `package.json` at build
time. The post-build check initializes a standalone copy containing only the built files.
The check requires the advertised version to match the package.
Therefore, a vendored build does not need a parent `package.json` at runtime.

The browser harness binds its temporary HTTP server to `127.0.0.1`. Viewer and
effect requests are confined to their configured roots after both lexical and
realpath checks. Dotfiles, dot-directories, traversal, and symlink escapes are
rejected. Responses no longer add wildcard CORS. Known asset extensions receive
explicit media types and unlisted extensions remain serveable as
`application/octet-stream`.

Successful file responses set `Vary: Origin`.
They echo `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only for these origins:

- An opaque `Origin: null`.
- An `http`/`https` loopback origin on `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, or `localhost`, with an optional port.

Other origins receive no allow-origin header.

Sources: `.mcp.json`; `.codex/config.toml`; Shade MCP `package.json`;
`src/index.ts` - registration and shutdown; `src/version.ts`;
`tsup.config.ts`; `scripts/check-dist-selfcontained.mjs`; `src/config.ts`;
`src/ai/provider.ts`; `src/harness/browser-session.ts`;
`src/harness/live-sessions.ts`; `src/harness/server-manager.ts`;
`src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - warmup timeout.

### Act

Shared input and batch behavior:

```ts
type EffectSelector = {
  effect_id?: string
  effects?: string // comma-separated IDs; takes precedence over effect_id
}

type BrowserSelector = EffectSelector & {
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // defaults to webgl2 where present
}

// Exactly one selected ID returns T; several return the batch envelope.
// Every T and every entry also carries `outcome: Outcome`.
type Batched<T> = T | {
  // "error" when every entry is an error; "fail" when any entry is fail or
  // error; "warning" when any is warning; "skipped" when all are skipped;
  // otherwise "ok"
  outcome: Outcome
  summary: { total: number, ok: number, fail: number, warning: number,
             skipped: number, error: number }
  results: T[]
}
type OuterEffectError = { effect_id: string, status: "error", error: string }
```

`effects` is split on commas and trimmed. Selectors are literal IDs; the tool
descriptions now specify comma-separated IDs without promising glob expansion.
With neither selector, `resolveEffectIds()` scans
`SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR`: one discovered effect is selected, multiple effects cause
an error, and a flat effect directory uses its basename. Filesystem analysis
tools reject absolute effect IDs and IDs containing `.` or `..` path segments
with `Invalid effect id: <id>` before reading. Browser selectors remain literal.

No numeric schema below uses Zod `.int()`, `.finite()`, `.min()`, `.max()`, or a
positive-resolution refinement unless explicitly stated. Descriptive ranges
are not validation, except in `runDslProgram`, whose bounds are enforced (see
its schema).

Browser verbs call `BrowserSession.setBackend()` before capture/compile work.
It now rejects a switch that does not reach the requested page backend.
`selectEffect()` waits for a post-selection graph and checks the page's current
effect identity; a missing or different identity fails closed. Browser results
report the page-confirmed backend and effect where available, including on
selection and switch failures.

#### compileEffect

```ts
type CompileEffectInput = EffectSelector & {
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
}

type CompileEffectResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok" | "error", backend: string,
      passes: Array<{ id: string, status: "ok" | "error",
                      errors?: string[] }>,
      message: string, console_errors?: string[] }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The tool waits for the selected effect's post-selection graph rather than
viewer status text, then reports its expanded passes. Passes without authored
names use `pass_<index>`; success message is `Compiled successfully`.
A compile failure is read from viewer status text containing the whole word
`error` or `failed`, so a success message naming an effect such as
`scanlineError` is not a failure. Backend-switch, selection, compile, and
missing page-identity failures return `status:"error"`, with the
page-confirmed effect/backend when available.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/compile.ts` - `compileEffectSchema`,
`compileEffect()`.

#### renderEffectFrame

```ts
type RenderEffectFrameInput = BrowserSelector & {
  warmup_frames?: number                 // default 10
  capture_image?: boolean                // default false
  uniforms?: Record<string, number>
  time?: number                          // seconds; timed capture (see below)
  resolution?: [number, number]
}

type RenderEffectFrameResult = Batched<RenderSuccess | RenderFailure>
```

With an explicit `time` the verb warms up while the loop is live, pauses at the
requested time, and redraws at that time before the readback, so the returned
frame is the requested paused frame and reproduces byte-identically per
requested time. Without
`time` the verb returns the live loop's last frame, nondeterministic with the
capture moment.

Metric definitions, ranges, and thresholds are in Rendered output. A captured
image is a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI. Otherwise `image_uri` is null.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts` -
`renderEffectFrameSchema`, `renderEffectFrame()`.

#### describeEffectFrame

```ts
type DescribeEffectFrameInput = EffectSelector & {
  prompt: string
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
  capture_image?: boolean         // default false
}

type DescribeEffectFrameResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok",
      frame?: { image_uri: string },
      vision: Record<string, JsonValue> | null }
  | { effect_id: string, status: "error", error: string }
>
```

The intended AI JSON is `{description,tags,notes}`, but a parsed object is not
schema-checked. A parsed primitive or array and invalid JSON instead produce
`{description:<text>,tags:[],notes:null}`. `frame` is omitted unless
`capture_image` is true, avoiding an unsolicited base64 payload. Failure strings
include the common no-key message, `Failed to render frame`, and
`Failed to render frame: <render error>`.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/describe.ts` - schema and
`describeEffectFrame()`; `src/ai/provider.ts` - provider/no-key behavior.

#### benchmarkEffectFPS

```ts
type BenchmarkEffectFPSInput = BrowserSelector & {
  target_fps?: number       // default 60
  duration_seconds?: number // default 5
  resolution?: [number, number]
}

type BenchmarkEffectFPSResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok", backend: string,
      requested_resolution?: [number, number],
      frame?: { width: number, height: number },
      warning?: string,
      achieved_fps: number,
      meets_target: boolean,
      stats: {
        frame_count: number,
        avg_frame_time_ms: number,
        jitter_ms: number,
        min_frame_time_ms: number,
        max_frame_time_ms: number
      }, console_errors?: string[] }
  // backend-switch or selection failure: zeroed measurement
  | { effect_id?: string, status: "error", backend: string, achieved_fps: 0,
      meets_target: false, stats: { frame_count: 0, avg_frame_time_ms: 0,
      jitter_ms: 0, min_frame_time_ms: 0, max_frame_time_ms: 0 }, error: string }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

`achieved_fps = frame_count/(sum(frame_times_ms)/1000)`, rounded to two
decimals, and `meets_target = achieved_fps >= target_fps` on that rounded
value. Jitter is sample standard deviation with divisor
`frame_count-1`, or zero for at most one frame. Reported values are rounded to
two decimals. Tool status remains `ok` when `meets_target` is false. Callers
must inspect the boolean.

The tool confirms the requested backend and effect before measurement and
reports the page-confirmed backend in its result.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/benchmark.ts` - schema and
`benchmarkEffectFPS()`.

#### testUniformResponsiveness

```ts
type TestUniformResponsivenessInput = BrowserSelector
type TestUniformResponsivenessResult = Batched<
  | ({ effect_id: string } & UniformResponsiveness)
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The test set, perturbation rule, `luma_diff > 0.002` and
`max_channel_diff > 0.002` thresholds, per-uniform measurements, and aggregate
status are in Parameters and globals. The tool confirms the requested backend
and effect before capture. WebGPU reads its offscreen surface through the
backend's async pixel reader after submitted work completes.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/uniforms.ts` - schema and
`testUniformResponsiveness()`.

#### testNoPassthrough

```ts
type TestNoPassthroughInput = BrowserSelector

type TestNoPassthroughResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok" | "passthrough",
      backend: string, isFilterEffect: true,
      similarity: number, threshold: 0.01, inputTexture: string,
      details: string,
      console_errors?: string[] }
  | { effect_id: string, status: "skipped" | "error",
      backend?: string, isFilterEffect: false, similarity: null, details: string,
      console_errors?: string[] }
  // a filter whose input or output texture could not be read
  | { effect_id: string, status: "error", backend: string,
      isFilterEffect: true, similarity: null, inputTexture?: string,
      details: string }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The tool classifies a filter by an expanded pass input key or value naming
`inputTex`, `inputTex3d`, or a user surface, including starter effects. It
renders at paused time zero, reads the consumed input texture (a `global_<name>` input through the half the
frame presented, then `global_<name>_read`) and the output surface through the
backend's async reader, and samples about 1000 pixels.
`similarity` is the normalized mean absolute RGB difference, despite its name:
the output modifies its input and returns `ok` only when `similarity > 0.01`.
Otherwise the status is `passthrough`. Nonfilters return `skipped` with `Not a
filter effect`. The comparison works on WebGL2 and WebGPU.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/passthrough.ts` - schema and
`testNoPassthrough()`.

#### testPixelParity

```ts
type TestPixelParityInput = EffectSelector & {
  epsilon?: number // default 1, described 0..255 but not range-checked
  seed?: number    // default 42
}

type TestPixelParityResult = Batched<
  ParitySuccessOrMismatch | ParityFailure | OuterEffectError
>
```

All output fields and predicates are in Cross-backend parity.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - schema and
`testPixelParity()`.

#### runDslProgram

```ts
type RunDslProgramInput = {
  dsl: string
  effects?: string               // comma-separated Portable package IDs
                                 // under SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR, max 16; omitted
                                 // means built-in effects only
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
  warmup_frames?: number         // integer, default 10 (0-120)
  frames?: number[]              // integers, default [1, 120, 600]; 1-6
                                 // strictly increasing values in 1-1200
  resolution?: [number, number]  // integers, default [960, 540];
                                 // 1-1920 x 1-1080
  cell_resolution?: [number, number] // integers, default [320, 180];
                                 // 1-1920 x 1-1080
  capture_image?: boolean        // legacy no-op: the grid is always returned
                                 // as MCP image content
  uniforms?: Record<string, number>
}

type RunDslProgramResult =
  | { status: "ok", backend: string,
      resolution: { width: number, height: number },
      warmup_frames: number, frames: number[],
      surfaces: string[], render_target: string,
      captures: Array<{ surface: string, frame: number,
                        width: number, height: number,
                        metrics: ImageMetrics }>,
      grid: { width: number, height: number, cell_width: number,
              cell_height: number, rows: string[], columns: number[] },
      frame: { width: number, height: number, image_uri: null },
      metrics: ImageMetrics,           // the final capture's metrics
      console_errors?: string[] }
  | { status: "error", error: string, console_errors?: string[] }
```

The verb renders in a fresh blank page: `CanvasRenderer` (and `compile`) is
imported from `SHADE_DSL_RENDERER_MODULE` (default `/shaders/src/index.js`
under `SHADE_VIEWER_ROOT`) with `SHADE_DSL_ASSETS_BASE` and
`SHADE_DSL_USE_BUNDLES` (defaults compatible with a Noisemaker repository
root), `renderer.compile(dsl)` runs the program, `renderer.stop()` ends the
loop, and each capture frame is read per written surface through the backend's
async `readPixels`. The whole batch is bounded by `session.timeoutMs`
(`SHADE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default `120000` ms). Each capture carries the full
`ImageMetrics` record; `metrics` repeats the final capture of the render
target. The per-surface PNG contact sheet (`grid` dimensions with
`cell_resolution` cells) is returned as the MCP `image` content block after
the JSON text block; `frame.image_uri` is always null (read the image content
instead). With `effects`, each listed Portable package is served at
`/effects/<id>`, its `definition.json` fetched, `definition.shaders` rebuilt
from the per-pass `glsl/`/`wgsl` program sources, and the raw Portable
definition registered live — this requires a Noisemaker renderer that
supports `registerPortableEffect` (present since the canvas-registration
change; built-in effect names stay protected and duplicate names are
rejected).

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/dsl.ts` - schema and `runDslProgram()`.

The worked example below records a complete paired source validation
exchange.

#### checkEffectStructure

```ts
type CheckEffectStructureInput = { effect_id: string }

type CheckEffectStructureResult =
  | { status: "ok" | "warning",
      unusedFiles: string[],
      namingIssues: Array<{ type: "func" | "global", name: string,
                            reason: "Must be camelCase" }>,
      nameCollisions: Array<{
        type: "uniform_function" | "reserved_word" | "builtin_shadow",
        name: string, file: string, message: string
      }>,
      leakedInternalUniforms: string[],
      missingDescription: boolean,
      structuralParityIssues: Array<{
        type: "missing_wgsl" | "missing_glsl", program: string, message: string
      }>,
      requiredUniformIssues: unknown[],
      multiPass: boolean,
      passCount: number,
      // set when the definition's passes are computed at run time; the
      // unused-file check was skipped and unusedFiles is empty
      unusedFilesUnchecked?: string }
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

Status is warning when any unused file, naming issue, name collision, leaked
internal uniform, missing description, or structural parity issue exists.
