`requiredUniformIssues` is initialized but never populated or included in the
status predicate. Pass `name` values are not checked. GLSL reserved/builtin
collision checks use regex-extracted declarations.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/structure.ts` -
`checkEffectStructure()`.

#### checkAlgEquiv

```ts
type CheckAlgEquivInput = { effect_id: string }

type CheckAlgEquivResult =
  | { status: "ok" | "divergent",
      pairs: Array<{
        program: string,
        parity: "equivalent" | "divergent" | "error" | string,
        confidence?: "high" | "medium" | "low" | string,
        notes?: string,
        concerns?: string[],
        [key: string]: unknown
      }>,
      unmatchedGlsl?: string[],
      unmatchedWgsl?: string[],
      summary: string }
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

Only same-stem `.glsl` and `.wgsl` files are paired. Split `.vert`/`.frag` files
are ignored. AI JSON is not schema-validated. Overall divergence counts only
entries whose `parity` is exactly `divergent`. AI parse/error entries can leave
overall status `ok`.

The handler writes the returned `program` after the parsed AI object.
Therefore, it always names the program matched by filename stem from disk, even if the model emits its own value. Errors include the no-key message, `Missing glsl/
or wgsl/ directory`, and `No matching GLSL/WGSL pairs found`.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/alg-equiv.ts` - `checkAlgEquiv()`.

#### compareShaders

```ts
type CompareShadersInput = { effect_id: string }

type ShaderStructure = {
  lines: number
  functions: string[]
  uniforms: string[]
}

type CompareShadersResult = {
  status: "ok"
  programs: Array<
    | { program: string, glsl: ShaderStructure, wgsl: ShaderStructure,
        lineDiff: number, functionCountDiff: number }
    | { program: string, glsl: ShaderStructure | null,
        wgsl: ShaderStructure | null,
        note: "No WGSL counterpart" | "No GLSL counterpart" }
  >
  summary: string
}
```

Only `.glsl` and `.wgsl` files are scanned. Function/uniform detection uses
regex after comment stripping. This tool always returns status `ok`, including
missing counterparts. Inspect `note` and null sides.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/compare.ts` - extractors and
`compareShaders()`.

#### analyzeBranching

```ts
type AnalyzeBranchingInput = {
  effect_id: string
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
}

type AnalyzeBranchingResult =
  | ({ status: "ok" | "warning" } & Record<string, JsonValue>)
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

GLSL mode reads `.glsl`. WebGPU reads `.wgsl`. AI output is not schema-
validated. The handler first computes `warning` when the sum of all returned
opportunity-array lengths is at least two and `ok` otherwise, irrespective of
severity.

Parsed AI JSON is spread first and the computed `status` is written
last, and the envelope computes `outcome` from that status, so neither a
model-provided `status`, `outcome`, nor `error` field changes the verdict. Callers must still
validate the untyped `shaders`, `opportunities`, and summary content before
using it. Errors before the AI call use `status:"error"` and include no AI key,
missing shader directory, and no shader files.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/branching.ts` -
`analyzeBranching()`.

#### searchEffects

```ts
type SearchEffectsInput = { query: string, limit?: number /* default 10 */ }
type SearchEffectsResult = {
  query: string
  results: Array<{ id: string, description: string,
                   tags: string[], score: number }>
  total: number
}
```

The query is lowercased, synonym-expanded, and whitespace-tokenized. Score is an unbounded sum of relevance weights:

- Full ID substring of the expanded query: +20 (a query with appended synonyms
  rarely matches).
- Per keyword: ID +8, name +15, description +5, tag +8, namespace +12.

Only positive scores are
returned, descending, sliced to `limit`. The shared effect index is rebuilt
after five seconds. Concurrent readers share one rebuild within the current
invalidation epoch. A `definition.json` that does not parse, or an effect
directory with no definition, is skipped with a server warning. A
`definition.js` that does not parse is listed with `func: "unknown"`, no
globals or passes, and `partial: true` with the parse error in
`partialReasons`. A build begun before explicit invalidation
cannot publish its stale index into the cache.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-effects.ts`;
`src/knowledge/effect-index.ts` - initialization and `search()`;
`src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` - cache lifetime and rebuild sharing.

#### analyzeEffect

```ts
type AnalyzeEffectInput = { effect_id: string }
type AnalyzeEffectResult =
  | { effectId: string, name?: string, description?: string,
      namespace?: string, tags: string[],
      globals: Record<string, unknown>, passes: Array<Record<string, unknown>>,
      format: "js" | "json", partial?: true, partialReasons?: string[],
      shaders: Record<`glsl/${string}.glsl` | `wgsl/${string}.wgsl`, string> }
  | { error: string }
```

For `definition.js`, Shade parses the module without running it and reads the
effect config as literal values, whether it is passed to `new Effect(...)` or
`super(...)` or written as class fields. Every global is returned, including
define-only globals, with `name` (the key), `type` (defaulting to `float`),
`uniform` (defaulting to the global's key), `default`, `min`, `max`, `step`,
`choices`, `control`, `define` and `ui`, and every pass with `name`,
`program` (defaulting to `main`), `type`, `inputs` and `outputs`. A value
computed at run time (a spread, `flatMap`, a reference to another binding) is
left out, and the result carries `partial: true` with `partialReasons` naming
each path. The projection does not carry Noisemaker-specific top-level fields
(`uniformLayout`, `paramAliases`, `textures`, ...) or global and pass fields
outside that set. Shader reads ignore split `.vert`/`.frag` files.
The repository's harness exposes the complete live schema:
`node shaders/tests/test-harness.js --describe <patterns>` (see below) returns
every authored definition field per effect, imported live, plus an audit of
what the Shade projection leaves out, with a corpus gate pinning that the
projection never contradicts the live definition.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/analyze-effect.ts`;
`src/formats/definition-js.ts` - `parseDefinitionJs()`.

#### searchShaderSource

```ts
type SearchShaderSourceInput = {
  query: string
  context_lines?: number // default 5
  limit?: number         // default 10
}
type SearchShaderSourceResult = {
  query: string
  matchCount: number
  results: Array<{
    effectId: string, file: string, lineNumber: number,
    matchLine: string, context: string
  }>
}
```

Only `.glsl` files are indexed. `query` is compiled case-insensitively as a
regular expression. Invalid regex syntax is escaped and treated literally.
Context line numbers are one-based. After a match, nearby lines equal to the
context window are skipped.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-source.ts`;
`src/knowledge/glsl-index.ts` - `search()`.

#### searchShaderKnowledge

```ts
type SearchShaderKnowledgeInput = {
  query: string
  category?: string
  limit?: number // default 5
}
type SearchShaderKnowledgeResult = {
  query: string
  category: string
  matchCount: number
  databaseStats: {
    totalDocuments: number, totalTerms: number, indexed: boolean,
    categories: Record<string, number>
  }
  results: Array<{
    title: string, category: string, score: number,
    snippet: string, tags?: string[], content?: string
  }>
}
```

Search uses synonym expansion and TF-IDF cosine similarity. Returned score is
rounded to three decimals and must be at least `0.05`. Cosine similarity is in
`[0,1]`. Full `content` is included only for the first three results.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-knowledge.ts`;
`src/knowledge/vector-db.ts` - `search()`, `getStats()`.

#### listEffects

```ts
type ListEffectsInput = { namespace?: string }
type ListEffectsResult = {
  namespace: string
  count: number
  effects: Array<{
    id: string, name: string | undefined, description: string,
    tags: string[], passes: number, partial?: true
  }>
}
```

Without a filter, `namespace` in output is `all`. The list uses Shade's lossy
definition projection. Pass counts and names reflect that parser, not imported
Noisemaker class instances. It shares the five-second refreshable effect index
with `searchEffects` and its invalidation-epoch behavior.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/utility/list-effects.ts`;

#### generateManifest

```ts
type GenerateManifestInput = Record<string, unknown> // schema has no properties and no additionalProperties:false; handler ignores args
type GenerateManifestResult =
  | { status: "ok", path: string, effectCount: number }
  | { error: string }
```

This verb writes `<SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR>/manifest.json` immediately with compact,
sorted JSON. It scans definition source with regexes for description, external
texture/mesh, tags, surface globals, and starter heuristics, and scans shader
files.

A successful write invalidates the cached effect index. A build already in
flight may return its own result to a caller waiting on that build, but it
cannot repopulate the shared cache after invalidation; the next list or search
starts a build for the new epoch.

This verb changes state. Do not call it during read-only introspection. The only explicit error is
`Effects directory not found: <path>`. Filesystem write exceptions escape the
handler.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/utility/generate-manifest.ts` -
`registerGenerateManifest()`; `src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` - invalidation.

### Validate

A tool exchange is protocol-valid when it returns an MCP result rather than a
JSON-RPC/MCP `error`. That is not tool or domain success. Treat
`result.isError === true` as a tool-call failure first. Its text is the JSON
error envelope. Otherwise, parse the JSON text; `outcome === "ok"` is the
common pass gate. Apply the predicate for that verb:

| Verb | Domain pass predicate |
|---|---|
| `compileEffect` | every result `status === "ok"` and every pass status `ok` |
| `renderEffectFrame` | status `ok`, then output metrics/harness exemptions |
| `describeEffectFrame` | status `ok` and required application-specific vision fields present |
| `benchmarkEffectFPS` | status `ok` and `meets_target === true` |
| `testUniformResponsiveness` | status `ok` and every entry ends `:pass` |
| `testNoPassthrough` | `ok`, or `skipped` only for a confirmed nonfilter |
| `testPixelParity` | status `ok`, no disallowed solid/Y-flip flags |
| `runDslProgram` | status `ok` with the full per-capture metric pass and the grid image |
| `checkEffectStructure` | status `ok`, all issue arrays empty, and no `unusedFilesUnchecked` (when it is present, unused files were not checked) |
| `checkAlgEquiv` | status `ok`, every pair exactly `equivalent`, no unmatched lists |
| `compareShaders` | both sides non-null and no `note` for every program |
| `analyzeBranching` | Validate the AI-derived fields. The tool returns `warning` when the opportunity count is `>=2`. Otherwise, it returns `ok`. |
| search/list/analyze | The requested record is present. These tools have no success status. |
| `generateManifest` | status `ok`, then independently inspect the written diff |

Batch callers must validate every `results` member; the batch `summary`
counts them by outcome. Never treat transport success,
outer `status:"ok"`, or a nonempty result as universal validation.
For every browser verb, including `testPixelParity`, check the page-confirmed
effect/backend fields and require domain success. The session now rejects a
failed backend switch or an effect selection without a confirmed new graph.

### Diagnose

Selector/scan failures thrown before per-effect loops include:

```text
Effects directory not found: <dir>. Specify effect_id or set SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR.
Failed to scan effects directory: <dir>
No effects found in <dir>. Specify effect_id.
Multiple effects found (<n>). Please specify effect_id or effects parameter. Available: ...
```

Browser tools catch per-effect exceptions as `OuterEffectError`.
Analysis/knowledge tools keep their own error payload forms
(`{status:"error",error}` or `{error}`), and every payload carries the common
`outcome` beside them. All 18 tools return through the shared `toolResult()`
envelope, and the server routes every handler through `guardToolErrors()`, so
an exception thrown before a handler's own error handling also returns the
JSON error envelope with `isError:true`.

AI-dependent tools use this exact no-key message:

```text
No AI API key found. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. Alternatively, create a .anthropic or .openai file in the project root.
```

Provider calls allow at most one retry. `describeEffectFrame` and
`checkAlgEquiv` request at most 1500 output tokens. `analyzeBranching` requests
at most 3000. Provider calls are bounded by `SHADE_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` as described
under Introspect.

Browser results can append `console_errors:string[]` through
`runWithConsoleCapture`, but field presence depends on the wrapper/result and
the messages are not categorized. Tool-specific failures are enumerated under
each verb above.

For `compileEffect`, `renderEffectFrame`, `describeEffectFrame`,
`benchmarkEffectFPS`, `testUniformResponsiveness`, `testNoPassthrough`, and
`testPixelParity`, the browser session waits for a graph built for the
requested effect and rejects an unconfirmed effect or backend. `runDslProgram`
uses a fresh renderer and reports its own backend. A tool call can still fail
through an outer browser/session error; inspect the returned status and
identity rather than treating transport success as validation.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/resolve-effects.ts`; all tool registration files;
`src/ai/provider.ts` - `NO_AI_KEY_MESSAGE`;
`src/harness/browser-session.ts` - console capture.

## Fully worked, source-complete effect and validation finding

This instance is the repository's `synth/testPattern` effect. The source
blocks below are complete, not excerpts. Its definition and shader files are
unchanged at the Noisemaker source snapshot named above. The current Shade MCP
release is the source commit and immutable pin named there. The effect declares
one pass; the DSL write to `o0` adds a terminal blit, yielding the two-pass
expanded graph shown below. The configured MCP session validates the requested
effect on both WebGL2 and WebGPU. Returned frame dimensions are authoritative;
the 256×256 request is rendered and returned at 256×256 (the demo viewer
presents it in a 90×90 canvas).

MCP request JSON is shown in wire order. Each response is the JSON value decoded
from the server's `content[0].text` field.

### Authoring inputs

export default new Effect({

<!-- WORKED:GLSL -->

`shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/glsl/testPattern.glsl`:

```glsl
#version 300 es
precision highp float;

uniform vec2 resolution;
uniform vec2 tileOffset;
uniform vec2 fullResolution;
uniform int gridSize;
uniform int pattern;

out vec4 fragColor;

// 3x5 pixel font for digits 0-9
// Each digit is encoded as 15 bits (3 columns x 5 rows, row-major)
const int GLYPH[10] = int[10](
    0x7B6F,  // 0: 111 101 101 101 111
    0x2492,  // 1: 010 010 010 010 010
    0x73E7,  // 2: 111 001 111 100 111
    0x72CF,  // 3: 111 001 011 001 111
    0x5BC9,  // 4: 101 101 111 001 001
    0x79CF,  // 5: 111 100 111 001 111
    0x79EF,  // 6: 111 100 111 101 111
    0x7249,  // 7: 111 001 001 001 001
    0x7BEF,  // 8: 111 101 111 101 111
    0x7BCF   // 9: 111 101 111 001 111
);

// Sample a glyph at local coordinates (0-2, 0-4)
bool sampleGlyph(int digit, int x, int y) {
    if (digit < 0 || digit > 9 || x < 0 || x > 2 || y < 0 || y > 4) return false;
    int bitIndex = y * 3 + (2 - x);  // row-major, top-left origin
    return ((GLYPH[digit] >> bitIndex) & 1) == 1;
}

// Render a number at a position within a cell
bool renderNumber(int number, vec2 cellUV) {
    // Determine how many digits we need
    int numDigits = 1;
    if (number >= 10) numDigits = 2;
    if (number >= 100) numDigits = 3;

    // Glyph dimensions in UV space (centered, cell-local)
    float glyphWidth = 0.15;
    float glyphHeight = 0.35;
    float spacing = 0.05;

    float totalWidth = float(numDigits) * glyphWidth + float(numDigits - 1) * spacing;
    float startX = 0.5 - totalWidth * 0.5;
    float startY = 0.5 - glyphHeight * 0.5;

    // Check if we're in the vertical range for glyphs
    if (cellUV.y < startY || cellUV.y >= startY + glyphHeight) return false;

    // Extract digits (right to left)
    int digits[3];
    int temp = number;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        digits[i] = temp % 10;
        temp /= 10;
    }

    // Check each digit position (left to right)
    for (int d = 0; d < numDigits; d++) {
        float digitX = startX + float(d) * (glyphWidth + spacing);

        if (cellUV.x >= digitX && cellUV.x < digitX + glyphWidth) {
            // We're in this digit's horizontal range
            float localX = (cellUV.x - digitX) / glyphWidth;
            float localY = (cellUV.y - startY) / glyphHeight;

            // Map to 3x5 grid
            int gx = int(localX * 3.0);
            int gy = int(localY * 5.0);

            // Get the correct digit (numDigits-1-d because digits[] is reversed)
            int digit = digits[numDigits - 1 - d];

            return sampleGlyph(digit, gx, gy);
        }
    }

    return false;
}

// Pattern 0: Numbered checkerboard
vec4 checkerboard(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    int cellX = int(uv.x * float(n)) % n;
    int cellY = int(uv.y * float(n)) % n;

    int cellNum = (n - 1 - cellY) * n + cellX;

    bool isWhiteCell = ((cellX + cellY) % 2) == 0;

    vec2 cellUV = fract(uv * float(n));

    bool isGlyph = renderNumber(cellNum, cellUV);

    float cellColor = isWhiteCell ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    float glyphColor = isWhiteCell ? 0.0 : 1.0;
    float finalColor = isGlyph ? glyphColor : cellColor;

    return vec4(vec3(finalColor), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 1: 8 vertical SMPTE-style color bars
vec4 colorBars(vec2 uv) {
    int bar = int(uv.x * 8.0);
    bar = clamp(bar, 0, 7);

    // white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, black
    vec3 colors[8] = vec3[8](
        vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3(1.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    );

    return vec4(colors[bar], 1.0);
}

// Pattern 2: Horizontal black-to-white gradient ramp
vec4 gradient(vec2 uv) {
    return vec4(vec3(uv.x), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 3: UV map (R=u, G=v, B=0)
vec4 uvMap(vec2 uv) {
    return vec4(uv.x, uv.y, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 4: Thin white grid lines on black
vec4 gridLines(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    vec2 cellUV = fract(uv * float(n));
    vec2 edge = min(cellUV, 1.0 - cellUV);

    // Use direct calculation instead of fwidth() for tile-aware rendering.
    // This maintains the same line thickness in normal rendering while ensuring
    // continuity across tile boundaries during large-format print export.
    vec2 fw = vec2(1.0) / fullResolution * float(n);

    float line = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 2.0 * fw.x, edge.x) * smoothstep(0.0, 2.0 * fw.y, edge.y);
    return vec4(vec3(line), 1.0);
}

// HSV to RGB (hue only, full saturation & value)
vec3 hue2rgb(float h) {
    float r = abs(h * 6.0 - 3.0) - 1.0;
    float g = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 2.0);
    float b = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 4.0);
    return clamp(vec3(r, g, b), 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 5: Each cell gets a unique hue
vec4 colorGrid(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    int cellX = int(uv.x * float(n)) % n;
    int cellY = int(uv.y * float(n)) % n;
    int cellIndex = cellY * n + cellX;
    float hue = fract(float(cellIndex) * 0.618033988749895);
    return vec4(hue2rgb(hue), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 6: Filled circle at each grid intersection
vec4 dotGrid(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    vec2 scaled = uv * float(n);
    vec2 nearest = round(scaled);
    float dist = length(scaled - nearest);
    float dot = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.12, 0.15, dist);
    return vec4(vec3(dot), 1.0);
}

void main() {
    vec2 globalCoord = gl_FragCoord.xy + tileOffset;
    vec2 uv = globalCoord / fullResolution;

    if (pattern == 1) {
        fragColor = colorBars(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 2) {
        fragColor = gradient(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 3) {
        fragColor = uvMap(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 4) {
        fragColor = gridLines(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 5) {
        fragColor = colorGrid(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 6) {
        fragColor = dotGrid(uv);
    } else {
        fragColor = checkerboard(uv);
    }
}
```

<!-- WORKED:WGSL -->

`shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/wgsl/testPattern.wgsl`:

```wgsl
// WGSL version – WebGPU

struct Uniforms {
    resolution: vec2f,
    gridSize: i32,
    pattern: i32,
    tileOffset: vec2f,
    fullResolution: vec2f,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> uniforms: Uniforms;

// 3x5 pixel font for digits 0-9
// Each digit is encoded as 15 bits (3 columns x 5 rows, row-major)
const GLYPH = array<i32, 10>(
    0x7B6F,  // 0: 111 101 101 101 111
    0x2492,  // 1: 010 010 010 010 010
    0x73E7,  // 2: 111 001 111 100 111
    0x72CF,  // 3: 111 001 011 001 111
    0x5BC9,  // 4: 101 101 111 001 001
    0x79CF,  // 5: 111 100 111 001 111
    0x79EF,  // 6: 111 100 111 101 111
    0x7249,  // 7: 111 001 001 001 001
    0x7BEF,  // 8: 111 101 111 101 111
    0x7BCF   // 9: 111 101 111 001 111
);

// Sample a glyph at local coordinates (0-2, 0-4)
fn sampleGlyph(digit: i32, x: i32, y: i32) -> bool {
    if (digit < 0 || digit > 9 || x < 0 || x > 2 || y < 0 || y > 4) {
        return false;
    }
    let bitIndex = y * 3 + (2 - x);  // row-major, top-left origin
    return ((GLYPH[digit] >> u32(bitIndex)) & 1) == 1;
}

// Render a number at a position within a cell
fn renderNumber(number: i32, cellUV: vec2f) -> bool {
    // Determine how many digits we need
    var numDigits = 1;
    if (number >= 10) { numDigits = 2; }
    if (number >= 100) { numDigits = 3; }

    // Glyph dimensions in UV space (centered, scaled to fit nicely)
    let glyphWidth = 0.15;
    let glyphHeight = 0.35;
    let spacing = 0.05;

    let totalWidth = f32(numDigits) * glyphWidth + f32(numDigits - 1) * spacing;
    let startX = 0.5 - totalWidth * 0.5;
    let startY = 0.5 - glyphHeight * 0.5;

    // Check if we're in the vertical range for glyphs
    if (cellUV.y < startY || cellUV.y >= startY + glyphHeight) {
        return false;
    }

    // Extract digits (right to left)
    var digits = array<i32, 3>(0, 0, 0);
    var temp = number;
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        digits[i] = temp % 10;
        temp = temp / 10;
    }

    // Check each digit position (left to right)
    for (var d = 0; d < numDigits; d++) {
        let digitX = startX + f32(d) * (glyphWidth + spacing);

        if (cellUV.x >= digitX && cellUV.x < digitX + glyphWidth) {
            // We're in this digit's horizontal range
            let localX = (cellUV.x - digitX) / glyphWidth;
            let localY = (cellUV.y - startY) / glyphHeight;

            // Map to 3x5 grid
            let gx = i32(localX * 3.0);
            let gy = i32(localY * 5.0);

            // Get the correct digit (numDigits-1-d because digits[] is reversed)
            let digit = digits[numDigits - 1 - d];

            return sampleGlyph(digit, gx, gy);
        }
    }

    return false;
}

// Pattern 0: Numbered checkerboard
fn checkerboard(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellX = i32(uv.x * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellY = i32(uv.y * f32(n)) % n;

    let cellNum = (n - 1 - cellY) * n + cellX;

    let isWhiteCell = ((cellX + cellY) % 2) == 0;

    let cellUV = fract(uv * f32(n));

    let isGlyph = renderNumber(cellNum, cellUV);

    let cellColor = select(0.0, 1.0, isWhiteCell);
    let glyphColor = select(1.0, 0.0, isWhiteCell);
    let finalColor = select(cellColor, glyphColor, isGlyph);

    return vec4f(vec3f(finalColor), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 1: 8 vertical SMPTE-style color bars
fn colorBars(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    var bar = i32(uv.x * 8.0);
    bar = clamp(bar, 0, 7);

    // white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, black
    let colors = array<vec3f, 8>(
        vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    );

    return vec4f(colors[bar], 1.0);
}

// Pattern 2: Horizontal black-to-white gradient ramp
fn gradientRamp(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    return vec4f(vec3f(uv.x), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 3: UV map (R=u, G=v, B=0)
fn uvMapPattern(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    return vec4f(uv.x, uv.y, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 4: Thin white grid lines on black
fn gridLines(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellUV = fract(uv * f32(n));
    let edge = min(cellUV, 1.0 - cellUV);
    // Non-tiling: original fwidth-based AA (byte-identical baseline).
    // Tiling: analytic AA width mirroring glsl/testPattern.glsl, which is
    // seam-stable across tiles where screen-space derivatives are not.
    let isTile = length(uniforms.tileOffset) > 0.0;
    // fwidthFine must be evaluated in uniform control flow (function scope),
    // so compute it unconditionally, then override only when tiling. The
    // analytic-width divide is skipped entirely on the non-tile path.
    var fw = fwidthFine(uv * f32(n));
    var edgeMul = 1.5;
    if (isTile) {
        let fr = select(uniforms.resolution, uniforms.fullResolution, uniforms.fullResolution.x > 0.0);
        fw = vec2f(1.0) / fr * f32(n);
        edgeMul = 2.0;
    }
    let line = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, edgeMul * fw.x, edge.x) * smoothstep(0.0, edgeMul * fw.y, edge.y);
    return vec4f(vec3f(line), 1.0);
}

// HSV to RGB (hue only, full saturation & value)
fn hue2rgb(h: f32) -> vec3f {
    let r = abs(h * 6.0 - 3.0) - 1.0;
    let g = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 2.0);
    let b = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 4.0);
    return clamp(vec3f(r, g, b), vec3f(0.0), vec3f(1.0));
}

// Pattern 5: Each cell gets a unique hue
fn colorGrid(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellX = i32(uv.x * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellY = i32(uv.y * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellIndex = cellY * n + cellX;
    let hue = fract(f32(cellIndex) * 0.618033988749895);
    return vec4f(hue2rgb(hue), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 6: Filled circle at each grid intersection
fn dotGrid(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let scaled = uv * f32(n);
    let nearest = round(scaled);
    let dist = length(scaled - nearest);
    let d = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.12, 0.15, dist);
    return vec4f(vec3f(d), 1.0);
}

@fragment
fn main(@builtin(position) position: vec4f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
    // Tile-aware global UV (mirror glsl/testPattern.glsl). Non-tiling
    // (tileOffset=(0,0), fullResolution=resolution) is byte-identical.
    let fr = select(uniforms.resolution, uniforms.fullResolution, uniforms.fullResolution.x > 0.0);
    let uv = (position.xy + uniforms.tileOffset) / fr;

    if (uniforms.pattern == 1) {
        return colorBars(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 2) {
        return gradientRamp(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 3) {
        return uvMapPattern(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 4) {
        return gridLines(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 5) {
        return colorGrid(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 6) {
        return dotGrid(uv);
    } else {
        return checkerboard(uv);
    }
}
```

The legal DSL invocation uses the generated enum identifier, writes the effect
chain to `o0`, and explicitly renders it:

```noisemaker
search synth
testPattern(pattern: checkerboard, gridSize: 4).write(o0)
render(o0)
```

`pattern` is a DSL `Identifier`, not the string literal `"checkerboard"`.
`gridSize` is a numeric expression. `compileGraph()` registers nothing: with
the checked-in effect registered first (`registerEffect()`, `registerOp()`,
`registerStarterOps()` and `mergeIntoEnums()`, as
`shaders/tests/test_contract_graph_shape.mjs` does), it expands this exact
program to two expanded passes:

```json
[
  {"id":"node_0_pass_0","program":"node_0_testPattern","inputs":{},"outputs":{"color":"node_0_out"}},
  {"id":"node_1_write_blit","program":"blit","type":"render","inputs":{"src":"node_0_out"},"outputs":{"color":"global_o0"}}
]
```

The first is the one declared effect pass. The second is the terminal write
blit. A direct `compileGraph()` invocation against the current pinned
Noisemaker source reproduced this exact pass array. No generator or repository
contract test on current
`main` locks the worked example to the document. Re-run the source-level check
under the freshness protocol when either pinned source changes.

Sources: `shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/definition.js` and its complete
GLSL/WGSL program files; `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` -
`registerEffectWithRuntime()` enum export; `shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` -
program expansion.

(`outcome:"skipped"`) because this is a source effect. On hosts where the
parity verb's browser cannot obtain a WebGPU adapter, its WebGPU leg fails

The structure scan has no issues and reports the one declared effect pass.
Both compile results report the two expanded passes and the page-confirmed
backend. The rendered frame is nonblank (`mean_alpha = 1`,
`luma_variance = 0.24998796755857344`) at the returned 256×256 resolution.
`gridSize` responds to the tested change (`luma_diff = 0.009534835815429688`,
above the `0.002` threshold). The parity comparison reports zero mismatches;
the benchmark meets 30 FPS at the 256×256 render size. These results apply to
the identified effect and backends.

Sources: the checked-in effect definition, shader programs, and graph expander;
Shade MCP browser tools and harness helpers at the pinned source commit.

## Surfaces x capabilities traceability matrix

<!-- TRACEABILITY-MATRIX -->

Every cell points to an executable contract or an explicitly identified gap.

| Surface | Introspect | Act | Validate | Diagnose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSL program | `Token`, `ParsedProgram`, `CompiledProgram`, registry keys, `CompiledGraph` | Complete EBNF plus call/read/write/render and nested-automation contracts | parse/unparse/compile and render metric predicates | `SyntaxError`, `Diagnostic`, `CompilationFailure` |
| Effect definition | `Effect` fields, registry/manifest, `checkEffectStructure` | `EffectDefinition` typed grammar | validator, structure scan, and page-confirmed browser selection | exact validator messages, structural arrays, backend and selection errors |
| Parameters and globals | `effect.globals`, transformed `uniforms`, registry params, MIDI/audio state and capture requirements | `GlobalSpec`, nested automation, and selected-input contracts | compile reflection, state-selection predicates, per-uniform numeric deltas | transform errors, type/range and capture failures |
| Passes and render graph | `Effect.passes`, `CompiledGraph.passes`, `CompiledGraph.textures`, `CompiledGraph.allocations` | `PassSpec` typed grammar, sampler/output binding rules, and MRT byte adaptation | graph analysis and per-pass compile, plus the queryable runtime allocation/reuse plan | unresolved inputs and backend compile/resource failures |
| Textures and surface resources | texture specs, `DeviceCapabilities`, and runtime surface dimensions/formats | `TextureSpec` typed grammar, exact accepted policies, and volume atlas clamp | allocation existence, size/format/limit inspection, render metrics | unsupported/missing surface failures and GL/device failures record structured `backend.diagnostics` entries (`ERR_MISSING_RENDER_TARGET`/`ERR_GL_ERROR`/`ERR_DEVICE_VALIDATION`); unknown-format/dimension fallbacks record `ERR_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_FALLBACK`/`ERR_DIMENSION_FALLBACK` |
| Compatibility and mutation | compiled AST, `listSteps`, `getCompatibleReplacements` | typed `replaceEffect` contract | candidate precheck and post-selection browser identity | compatibility and transform errors |
| Rendered output | frame dimensions, `ImageMetrics`, sink stats, and `PackedFrame` | `RenderEffectFrameInput`, `Sink`, and `FrameExportQueue` contracts | exact metric predicates plus bounded queue/accounting rules | metric, capture, sink, and export failures |
| Cross-backend parity | source-pair availability and parity report | GLSL ES 3.00/WGSL authoring contracts | buffer diff predicates with confirmed effect/backend on both legs | compile/readback/divergence reports |
| Shade MCP tool contracts | `tools/list`, effect scanners, all output types | Full signatures for all 18 verbs | verb-specific domain predicates | the common `outcome` envelope, selector errors and tool-specific fields |

External ports are deliberately outside this matrix. Their repositories define
separate candidate renderers, golden-image comparators, tolerance policies, and
failure reports. This document makes no cross-runtime validation claim for
those ports.

The matrix has 9 surfaces x 4 capabilities = 36 filled cells.
